sources.title: Tele2: RCS on iPhone and Android
sources.finding: Tele2 states on its support page that RCS can be used on iPhone and Android when the right conditions are met.
sources.implication: The statement covers the operator's description of private chat. Check your own subscription and business reach separately.

sources.title: Comviq: RCS on iPhone and Android
sources.finding: Comviq describes RCS on iPhone and Android on its support page.
sources.implication: Go by Comviq's answer for your number, not only by which network the operator uses.

sources.title: Apple: Carrier support in Europe
sources.finding: Apple publishes carrier features by country and carrier in its European support list.
sources.implication: Read the right country section and compare it with the carrier's own information. A list entry does not settle business reach.

sources.title: Apple: iMessage, RCS and SMS/MMS
sources.finding: Apple's Messages can use iMessage, RCS and SMS/MMS. RCS and SMS can both appear with green bubbles.
sources.implication: The bubble color does not tell RCS from SMS; the channel text in the conversation gives better information.

sources.title: Google RCS for Business: Receive messages
sources.finding: Google documents incoming customer messages, including text and media content.
sources.implication: Receive and assess the customer's actual reply; a button-driven dialog also needs to handle other content.

sources.title: Google RCS for Business: Launch details
sources.finding: Google has separate launch details and launch status for business agents.
sources.implication: A test agent that has been created is not the same as a sender approved for public sends.

sources.title: Google RCS for Business: Analytics
sources.finding: Google has separate documentation for measurement in RCS for Business.
sources.implication: Read the definitions behind the report. Channel statistics and purchase data come from different sources and need to be linked for business analysis.

sources.title: IMY: The right to object
sources.finding: IMY states that the data subject can always object to the processing of personal data for direct marketing.
sources.implication: An objection must take effect in the sending systems. This right alone does not answer questions about retention periods or other legal bases.

sources.title: Konsumentverket: The Marketing Act
sources.finding: Konsumentverket describes requirements including identification of advertising and that marketing must not be misleading.
sources.implication: A new message format does not change the requirements for a clear sender or for evidence of claimed customer results.

sources.title: GSMA: RCS Universal Profile
sources.finding: Universal Profile is GSMA's common technical foundation for RCS.
sources.implication: A common standard does not mean that every carrier or app has introduced the same features.

sources.title: Google Messages: Common questions about RCS chats
sources.finding: Google Messages uses Wi-Fi or mobile data for RCS and shows the connection status in the app.
sources.implication: Check both the connection and the channel in the conversation in question; having the setting turned on is not enough.

sources.title: Google Messages: RCS chats with businesses
sources.finding: Google describes business RCS separately from private chats, with a business profile and the option to block the sender.
sources.implication: Private RCS support should not be used as proof that a given business sender reaches the customer.

sources.title: Apple: About RCS messages on iPhone
sources.finding: Apple lists iOS 18 or later and a carrier with RCS support as requirements on iPhone.
sources.implication: The system version alone gives no reliable answer about support on a Swedish subscription or for business sends.

sources.title: Google Messages: How RCS chats protect your conversations
sources.finding: Google describes end-to-end encryption for eligible private RCS conversations in Google Messages.
sources.implication: That protection should not be assumed for business RCS. Sender verification and encryption are different things.

sources.title: Google RCS for Business: Create an agent
sources.finding: In Google's business model, the sender is represented by an agent with brand and contact details.
sources.implication: The agent is a registered sender, not automatically a chatbot or AI. The customer's systems control what it does.

sources.title: Google RCS for Business: Brand verification
sources.finding: Google's brand verification checks the brand and the partner's authorization before launch.
sources.implication: An approved identity is neither a quality certificate for the offer nor permission to contact every recipient.

sources.title: Google RCS for Business: Rich cards
sources.finding: Google documents rich cards with media, title, description and suggestions, as well as carousels of cards.
sources.implication: Choose the format based on the content and test it on recipient devices. A richer format does not by itself give a better result.

sources.title: Google RCS for Business: What can agents do?
sources.finding: Google distinguishes suggested replies from actions such as opening a web address.
sources.implication: A sent reply and a visit to a website are different events. A completed booking must be confirmed in the booking system.

sources.title: Google RCS for Business: Send messages
sources.finding: Google documents sending, error handling and limitations for its RCS for Business service.
sources.implication: Use the documentation for your actual provider. That a request was accepted is not a delivery confirmation.

sources.title: Google RCS for Business: Receive events
sources.finding: Google distinguishes the delivery event DELIVERED from the read event READ for business messages.
sources.implication: The statuses describe different steps. Neither delivery nor reading proves understanding, consent or a purchase.

sources.title: Google RCS for Business: Webhooks
sources.finding: Google's business RCS sends incoming messages and events to a configured webhook.
sources.implication: The receiver needs to verify requests and handle redeliveries without changing the same customer case more than once.

sources.title: Google RCS for Business: Capability checks
sources.finding: Google's capability check examines reach and supported features for a phone number and a business agent.
sources.implication: It is more specific than phone model or carrier name, but it is not a receipt for a later send.

sources.title: Google RCS for Business: Best practices
sources.finding: Google recommends relevant messages, clear user choices and respect for the recipient's wishes.
sources.implication: This is guidance, not a measured campaign result. The effect needs to be followed in your own customer journey.

sources.title: Bandwidth: Updates to RCS for Business agent logos in Google Messages
sources.finding: Bandwidth writes that Google Messages shows logos for RCS businesses as rounded squares instead of circles, that verified senders get a checkmark after the name, and that the logo should be 224 × 224 px with a solid background. All logos must be updated by June 1, 2027.
sources.implication: The information comes from a provider's customer notice about Google's change, not from a measurement. Check the requirements with your partner before changing the logo.

glossary.definition: An agent is the company's sender on Google's RCS platform. It represents the brand in the messaging app and can be connected to the company's systems.
The agent profile is the business information shown for the RCS sender, such as name and logo. The customer should be able to recognize who is getting in touch.
An API lets one system request things from a service. In an RCS flow, the order system can use it to ask for a message when an order is shipped.
Asynchronous delivery means a message is handled after the first request. The system can get a response from the API before the customer has received the message.
Brand verification is Google's check of the link between an RCS agent and the brand it represents. An authorized representative confirms the details and the partner's right to manage the sender.
A check of whether a recipient can communicate with an RBM agent and which features are supported. Support for the channel and support for a specific feature are different questions.
A switch to an alternative channel when the first one cannot be used under the flow's conditions. SMS fallback must be confirmed with the provider and is not automatically part of every RCS service.
A suggested action is a button that helps the customer do something, such as open a website. In Swedish it is called föreslagen åtgärd.
A pre-written reply option that the recipient can select. The agent's system can receive an event with the selected reply and its associated data.
An RCS carousel is several message cards that the customer can scroll between. It can show products or other options with matching information on each card.
A delivery receipt reports that a message was delivered to the recipient's device according to the service's status model. It comes after the send was requested.
A read receipt is the messaging app's report of read status. It can help the company follow a send, but does not show that the customer understood or approved the message.
MaaP stands for Messaging as a Platform. It is a GSMA term for the platform support behind business communication via RCS.
MMS stands for Multimedia Messaging Service and is a service for messages with, for example, images. MMS and RCS can appear in the same app but are different technologies.
The mobile carrier provides your subscription and can affect which RCS features can be used. This is especially noticeable when iPhone needs carrier support.
P2P means person to person. In RCS it refers to private chat, for example when two people write to each other in Google Messages.
Postback data is information that accompanies the customer's selection of a reply or an action. The company's system can use it to understand which choice was made.

glossary.aliases: rcs business messaging rcs for business
glossary.definition: RBM stands for RCS Business Messaging, that is, the business use of RCS. The company can send content under a registered sender and receive customer replies.
Rich Communication Services. A messaging standard with support for more features than text alone. RCS is not the name of a single app or a uniform provider service.
An RCS chat is a conversation that uses RCS over Wi-Fi or mobile data. Where supported, participants can share images, see read receipts and see when someone is typing.
An RCS client is the app that handles RCS on the phone. Google Messages and Apple's Messages are examples of apps that can use the technology.
A rich card is a structured RCS card with room for media, a title, a description and choices. It can, for example, present a product with an image and a link.
A typing indicator shows that the other person is typing in an RCS chat. It says nothing about which reply is coming or whether anything is sent.
SMS stands for Short Message Service and is the service for ordinary text messages over the mobile network. It does not need an active internet connection.
GSMA's industry-agreed set of RCS features and technical requirements. The common foundation is not a promise of identical functionality on all devices.
A business sender whose identity and authorization have been approved under a defined process. Verification should not be confused with encryption or a guarantee of the content of every message.
A webhook is an HTTPS address that receives events from a service. In RCS it can be a delivery status or a customer reply that needs to be passed on to your system.

articles.title: What is RCS?
articles.description: RCS is a messaging standard that lets you send text, images and files over the internet in your phone's messaging app. The name stands for Rich Communication Services. This means you do not need a separate RCS app.

paragraphs: When both participants have support, the chat can show read receipts and when the other person is typing. The same app can also send SMS or MMS, so not every message in it necessarily uses RCS.

Businesses can use a registered sender with a name and logo and send images or reply buttons. That service has its own requirements for registration and reach. A private RCS conversation and a business message therefore need to be assessed separately.

sections.title: What does the recipient notice?
paragraphs: You can start a conversation in the regular inbox and still get different features depending on who you write to. RCS is therefore best understood as the way the message is transported and displayed. It does not add a new contact list. For businesses, a registered profile and a system that handles sending and replies are also needed. The customer does not have to install the company's own app to read the message.

articles.title: How is RCS different from SMS and MMS?
articles.description: SMS is text messaging over the mobile network. MMS can also contain images. RCS uses wifi or mobile data and can offer better media sharing, read receipts and interactive business messages.

paragraphs: All three can be shown in the same app, without a new inbox. The difference shows up when you send content or check status.

A single SMS normally holds 160 GSM-7 characters. Other characters or longer text can result in several parts. For businesses that want to use SMS when RCS does not work, a confirmed fallback and a separate SMS text are needed.

sections.title: Choose the channel for the task
paragraphs: A short message without an image or reply options can work well as an SMS. RCS becomes more interesting when the customer needs to see something or make a clear choice directly in the message. Compare the same task in both channels. If the RCS version shows three products, the SMS version may need to link to a page where the same products can be compared, rather than trying to reproduce the whole carousel in text.

articles.title: What is RCS for business?
articles.description: RCS for business lets a registered sender send messages with a company profile, images and selectable replies in the customer's messaging app. It is often called RCS Business Messaging, RBM.

paragraphs: A web shop can let its order system send a delivery message with a tracking button. A web interface suits cases where a person wants to create a mailing manually. RCS is the channel. The order status and the handling of customer replies live in the company's own systems.

Before sending, the sender needs to be approved and the service needs to be able to reach the customers. Registration does not give you the right to market to anyone. Contact rules and any SMS fallback also need to be in place.

sections.title: The channel needs a context
paragraphs: A business message is useful when it relates to something the customer already understands: an order, a booking or a question. Also plan who owns the next step. A reply about a changed delivery should reach delivery handling and not get stuck in a separate inbox. Choosing RCS solves how the message looks on the phone. The routine behind the message decides whether the customer actually gets help.

articles.title: What does a verified sender mean?
articles.description: Verification checks the link between the RCS sender and the brand it represents. In Google Messages, the customer can see the company name, logo and a verification mark.

paragraphs: In Google's process, an authorized representative confirms the details and that the partner may manage the sender. This is done before launch. Ask your partner which documents are needed and which markets the approval covers.

The mark helps the customer recognize the company, but it is not a quality seal for every offer or link. It also says nothing about end-to-end encryption. An unexpected request for payment or sensitive information should still be checked.

sections.title: Recognition without false security
paragraphs: The profile name should be the one the customer recognizes from the purchase. An unfamiliar group name can create uncertainty even when it is correctly registered. Keep the logo, contact paths and link domains consistent. If the brand changes, the details need to be reviewed with the partner. The customer should be able to verify the sender through an independent contact path, especially when the message concerns money or account details.

articles.title: What are rich cards and carousels?
articles.description: A rich card is a message card that can combine an image, a heading, a description and buttons. A carousel is several such cards that the customer swipes between, for example a selection of products.

paragraphs: One card suits a single, self-contained message. Several cards suit cases where the options are meant to be compared. Do not put the customer's booking time on the last card. It should be easy to find right away.

Buttons can send a suggested reply or open, for example, a website. These are different actions that need to be handled correctly. Check recipient support and write a simpler fallback text if the flow will also use SMS.

sections.title: One choice per card
paragraphs: A carousel works best when the cards follow the same structure: image, understandable name, relevant detail and next step. If every card has a new layout, the options become harder to compare. A single rich card is often better for a delivery or booking. Start with the content the customer needs, and add more cards only when they represent real options.

articles.title: How do RCS APIs and webhooks work?
articles.description: An RCS API lets your systems request a message to be sent. Webhooks receive later events such as delivery, read status and customer replies. The API accepting the request does not yet mean the phone has received the message.

paragraphs: Store the message identifier together with the order or case. When an event comes back, you can then update the right record. Verify the origin of the webhook call before the event is processed.

Addresses, fields and authentication depend on the provider. Use the documentation for the service you connect to. If SMS is to be the fallback, the integration also needs to know when it may be sent and how a pending RCS message is handled without sending duplicates.

sections.title: Two directions in the same flow
paragraphs: The send request and the reply live for different lengths of time. An order system can request the message now while the phone's delivery report arrives later. The integration therefore needs to be able to find the same order without the original call still being open. Describe what each status may change and what should happen if an event is missing. This makes troubleshooting much clearer than a single label that says sent.

articles.title: What does RCS on iPhone require?
articles.description: RCS can be used in the iPhone Messages app from iOS 18, but the carrier and the plan must also support it. A system update alone is not enough.

paragraphs: Look under Settings, Apps, Messages for RCS messaging. If the option is missing, ask the carrier about your specific line. When it works, a conversation with an Android user can get better image sharing and read receipts.

Check the channel label in the conversation itself. Green bubbles can be both RCS and SMS. Businesses that want to reach iPhone users should also test their registered sender, since a private chat does not show the full business reach.

sections.title: Test a real conversation
paragraphs: Once the setting is there, open a conversation with someone who has confirmed RCS and check the channel label before you send. A successful image message is not proof on its own, because MMS can also carry images. If RCS is missing, note the iOS version and which line is used. For a business sender, a separate test from that specific agent is also needed, not only between two private phones.

articles.title: How does RCS work on Android?
articles.description: On Android, RCS is often used in Google Messages. When the app is connected, it can send over wifi or mobile data and show read receipts and typing indicators where supported.

paragraphs: Tap your profile picture and open the message settings, then RCS chats. There you can see the connection status and which number is used.
The person you write to also needs RCS. Otherwise the conversation may use SMS or MMS. Resending depends on the app's settings and access to the right network, and it is not a delivery guarantee.

sections.title: App, number and connection
paragraphs: A phone can have several messaging apps, but it is the settings in the app you use that matter. Check that the right number is shown under RCS chats and that the connection is ready. If a particular conversation still goes as SMS, the cause may be on the recipient's side. Do not change the whole phone's configuration just because one contact lacks support.

articles.title: How do I turn on RCS?
articles.description: You turn on RCS in the messaging app's settings. The phone needs internet, correct number registration and support for the feature.

paragraphs: On Android: open Google Messages, tap your profile picture and choose message settings, then RCS chats. Turn the feature on and check that the status becomes connected.
On iPhone: open Settings, Apps, Messages and turn on RCS messaging if the option is there. If it is missing, the carrier needs to confirm support for your plan.
Try it with someone who already has working RCS. If the connection gets stuck, check the number, the internet connection and app updates before you follow the official troubleshooting.

sections.title: When turning it on is not enough
paragraphs: Distinguish between the feature being switched on and the registration being finished. A verifying status means the app is still trying to link the service to the number. Read the current status before you test again. Repeatedly switching it off and on gives no clear basis for troubleshooting. Once the connection is ready, the other participant also needs support for the conversation to use RCS.

articles.title: What does RCS cost?
articles.description: Private RCS uses wifi or mobile data. The cost therefore follows your connection. Business messages have separate pricing from the service that sends them.

paragraphs: At rcsdirekt.se, Basic costs from 0.316 SEK, Single from 0.462 SEK and Conversation from 0.641 SEK per message. You pay per message with no monthly fee or commitment period.
Count the number of messages per type when you estimate a campaign. Check separately what any SMS fallback costs, and include integration and handling if you want to calculate the full project cost.

sections.title: Calculate what will be sent
paragraphs: Two projects with the same number of customers can have different costs if one sends a single message and the other sends several follow-ups. Base the budget on messages, not only on the size of the contact list. Also separate the price of the channel from the work of producing content and connecting order systems. Any fallback channel should be counted separately so the cost is not hidden in an average.

articles.title: Is RCS secure?
articles.description: It depends on which RCS service and which protection you mean. Verification helps identify the business sender. Encryption protects the content of the message. They solve different problems.

paragraphs: Google describes end-to-end encryption for some private RCS chats. That protection should not be assumed to apply to all business messages. A verification mark also does not mean that every link from the company is safe.
For a business flow, you need to know how data is protected both in the channel and in your own systems. Do not send passwords, and choose a suitably protected route for sensitive information.

sections.title: Assess the whole information path
paragraphs: A link can lead from the message to a website where the customer logs in. The security of that website and the permissions in the company's system then matter too. Limit the information shown on the lock screen and avoid turning the chat into storage for sensitive documents. Ask the provider which protection applies to business messages and stored customer replies, instead of settling for the word encrypted.

articles.title: How did RCS develop?
articles.description: RCS was developed within the mobile industry to give messages more features than SMS and MMS. The GSMA Universal Profile became a common technical foundation for apps, networks and services.

paragraphs: The standard is not an app. Carriers and app developers introduce support in their services, which is one reason availability can differ between phones and countries.
RCS is available in Google Messages and can be used in Apple's Messages with the right carrier support. For a planned campaign, today's reach matters more than the age of the standard.

sections.title: Why the rollout happens in stages
paragraphs: A standard becomes useful only when networks, apps and sender services support it. These parts are not updated at the same time, which explains why a launch in one country says nothing automatic about another. The history helps you understand the differences, but it is not an availability list. When buying, it is better to ask for a current reach test than to rely on an old launch year.

articles.title: What is Universal Profile?
articles.description: Universal Profile is the GSMA's common set of features and technical requirements for RCS. It is meant to make it easier for different apps, networks and services to communicate.

paragraphs: It is a technical foundation. It is not a subscription or a promise of identical appearance on every phone. Versions and implementations can support different features.
If you want to send a carousel or use a certain button, your service and the recipient still need to support that specific feature.

sections.title: Version is not the same as reach
paragraphs: Two services can refer to Universal Profile and still have different features implemented. This can show up in media, buttons or how a conversation is displayed. When a provider describes standard support, the question should therefore be followed by what actually works for your recipients. A practical test of the planned content gives more useful information than a version number without explanation.

articles.title: Does RCS need internet?
articles.description: Yes, RCS needs internet over wifi or mobile data. A message to a recipient without a connection may have to wait or be sent through another channel.

paragraphs: Google Messages can resend as SMS or MMS when the settings allow it. That channel also needs to work, so SMS does not solve every coverage problem.

For businesses, an SMS fallback should be available in the service or the integration. Also decide when the message becomes too old to send. A reminder after the booking has passed is no longer useful.

sections.title: Connectivity and timeliness
paragraphs: A message can stay queued while the phone has no internet. When the connection returns, the content may already be out of date, for example a reminder about a time that has passed. For time-sensitive business messages, you need to decide how long the information remains useful. A wifi test shows that the connection works at that moment, but says nothing about how delivery behaves when the customer is offline later.

articles.title: What are the misunderstandings about RCS?
articles.description: RCS is neither an app of its own nor a guarantee that all messages have the same features. It is a standard used by different apps and services.

paragraphs: Two common misunderstandings concern iPhone and encryption. RCS can work on iPhone with carrier support. End-to-end encryption exists for some private chats, but should not be assumed to protect all business messages.
RCS has also not replaced SMS everywhere. An SMS fallback needs to be arranged for business flows, and a private chat over wifi says nothing about the price of a business message.

sections.title: Examine what a claim refers to
paragraphs: When someone says RCS is on all new phones, several conditions are often missing: app, carrier, setting and business sender. Ask for a concrete use case before the claim becomes a planning basis. The same goes for results such as a higher click rate. A single campaign outcome is not a property of the standard and needs to be described with the audience, comparison and measurement method.

articles.title: What do the RCS terms mean in Swedish?
articles.description: Agent means business sender, rich card is a message card and carousel is several cards you can swipe between. The words describe parts of RCS. None of them is an app of its own.

paragraphs: Suggested reply is a ready-made answer the customer sends back. Suggested action is an action, for example opening a link. A reply and an opened website need to be handled differently.
Fallback means a backup channel, often SMS. A webhook receives events such as delivery status or customer replies and can pass them on to the right case in the company's system.

sections.title: Translate into what happens
paragraphs: Technical words become easier to understand when they are tied to an action. The agent is who the customer sees as the sender, the card is the content and the webhook is the way back to the company's systems. Postback data helps the system recognize a choice. These parts can be used together, but they do not replace each other. A nice profile says nothing, for example, about how an incoming customer reply is handled.

articles.title: How is RCS used in marketing?
articles.description: RCS can show an offer with a company name, image and buttons in the customer's messaging app. A card can present a product, and a carousel can give several options.

paragraphs: Write what the offer covers and where the button leads. Too many choices or a long introduction can make the message harder to understand, even in a rich format.

Check contact rules, opt-out and recipient support before sending. Follow up on the result on the page where the customer buys or books. Clicks show interest, but the format gives no guaranteed sales increase.

sections.title: From offer to result
paragraphs: Decide whether the goal is a page visit, a booking or a purchase before you design the message. A button that opens the campaign page should be followed by a page where the offer still applies and can be completed. If the customer has to search for the same product again, the message has only moved the friction. Evaluate the whole path and keep your conclusions to what you have actually measured.

articles.title: How can e-commerce businesses use RCS?
articles.description: E-commerce businesses can use RCS for order confirmations, delivery status and product display. A delivery message can combine the order reference, current status and a tracking link.

paragraphs: Use the company name the customer recognizes and fetch the details from the right order. A registered profile does not help if the link opens the wrong order.
Keep service messages and advertising separate. They have different purposes and can have different contact rules. For important messages, you also need to know how customers without RCS are reached.

sections.title: Let the order drive the message
paragraphs: The message should be based on a defined event in the order flow. If an order is split into several parcels, the customer needs to understand which part the message concerns. It is also important that older statuses are not overwritten by later incoming message events. RCS can make the information easier to read, but accuracy comes from the order and delivery systems that feed the flow.

articles.title: How is RCS used in customer service?
articles.description: With RCS, the customer can write to the company or choose a ready-made reply in the messaging app. Staff or a connected system must then take care of the question.

paragraphs: Buttons suit cases where the options are clear, such as order status or a request to reschedule. Let the customer reach a person when no option helps.
Confirm what has happened. We have received your request means something different from Your appointment has been rescheduled. Link the reply to the case system so that the message is accurate.

sections.title: Replies need an owner
paragraphs: A customer who writes in the chat expects the question to reach someone. State what happens outside staffed hours and let ongoing cases follow along to staff. If the customer has already explained the problem, the handover should not require the same story again. Measure the time to a meaningful reply, and not only how fast an automatic acknowledgment is sent.

articles.title: How do booking reminders work with RCS?
articles.description: An RCS reminder can show the booked time and let the customer confirm or ask to reschedule. The choice is simple, but the booking system needs to handle the reply.

paragraphs: Show the date, time and place directly. If a reschedule must be handled by staff, the first reply should confirm the request and should not claim that a new time is ready.
Avoid sensitive details in the reminder. Set a relevant validity period and plan any SMS fallback so that the customer does not get duplicate or outdated messages.

sections.title: Confirming and changing are different things
paragraphs: A button that confirms attendance can be handled directly if the booking system supports it. A reschedule, on the other hand, may require new choices or a decision from staff. State that difference clearly in the message after the button press. If a booking is changed in the meantime, the next message should use the new time, and not a copy of the information that existed when the reminder was scheduled.

articles.title: How are delivery notifications sent with RCS?
articles.description: An RCS delivery notification can show the current status, a time window and a tracking link under the company's registered name. The customer should be able to see right away which order it is about.

paragraphs: Tell apart an order that is being packed, one that has been shipped and one that is expected to arrive. The information has to come from the delivery system; the message format does not change the status of the transport.
Use a clear link to the right delivery. If your service offers it, prepare a fallback for important notifications, but do not count on any channel as an unconditional delivery guarantee.

sections.title: Several messages about the same delivery
paragraphs: The customer does not need a new message for every internal status change. Choose events that change what the customer needs to know or do. A delay notice is useful, for example, if it shows a new time window and a working way to get in touch. Tie the message to the delivery reference so that one tap opens the right shipment, even when the customer has several orders.

articles.title: How can restaurants use RCS?
articles.description: A restaurant can send booking confirmations, show a menu with images or make an offer via RCS. A button can open the booking page or help the customer contact the restaurant.

paragraphs: A booking confirmation needs the time, the place and any conditions. A menu image can show the food, but important information should also be readable as text.

A new offer is marketing and should be assessed separately from the booking. Check that the customer may be contacted and can unsubscribe. A button to the booking page does not mean the table is already booked.

sections.title: Make the booking easy to find
paragraphs: A guest on the way to the restaurant gets more use from the time, the address and a way to get in touch than from several menu images. Put the most important things first and let a map or a booking link complement the text. If someone replies with allergy questions or a change in party size, the restaurant needs a routine for that. A rich message should not invite replies that nobody then reads.

articles.title: Which rules apply to RCS campaigns?
articles.description: The company is responsible for personal data and contact rules even when the campaign uses RCS. Phone numbers, replies and delivery data can be personal data if they can be linked to a person.

paragraphs: The GDPR legal basis for the processing and the rules on marketing contact are separate questions. A booking confirmation and an advertising offer therefore have to be assessed according to their respective purposes.

Inform the recipient and limit what you store and for how long. Unsubscribing needs to work in the systems that control the campaigns. Have an adviser who knows data protection assess your setup; this overview does not replace legal advice.

sections.title: Keep the purposes apart
paragraphs: The same phone number can be in both a booking register and a campaign list without the use being the same. Document why the data is needed in each flow and how the recipient's choice takes effect. A technical delivery receipt can be used for troubleshooting but should not automatically become a new basis for marketing. The assessment of legal basis, information and contact rules has to be made for the actual processing.

articles.title: How do I measure the results of RCS?
articles.description: ROI compares the value of a result with the cost of achieving it. RCS can provide delivery and read data, but a read receipt or a click is not a completed purchase.

paragraphs: If the goal is bookings, the completed bookings need to be tracked in the booking system. Delivery, reads and clicks can show where customers drop off on the way there.
Compare equivalent groups and include messages, integration and handling in the cost. Test one clear change at a time so it is possible to understand what affected the outcome.

sections.title: Results need a comparison
paragraphs: If a campaign produces more bookings, you need to know what would have happened without it. A comparable control group or a well-designed test can give better support than comparing two different seasons. Costs and revenue should cover the same period. Do not count every click as a customer or every booking as revenue if cancellations and refunds are not yet known.

articles.title: How do I plan an RCS campaign?
articles.description: An RCS campaign needs a goal, relevant recipients and a message that can be acted on. Choose the format by what the customer should do, and pay less attention to how many features exist.

paragraphs: A first test can have one offer and one link. Decide how the result will be followed up and check that the sender is launched and the contact is permitted.
Try the links, replies, validity period and any fallback version before you send widely. The message is not finished until the next step also works for the customer.

sections.title: Plan the next step before sending
paragraphs: A message can be finished while the campaign is still not ready. The landing page has to be able to handle the traffic and the staff have to know how customer replies are handled. Also decide who is allowed to pause the campaign if something goes wrong. A small first test can then be used to find real problems in the flow, and the test is then about more than how the image looks.

articles.title: What tone suits RCS?
articles.description: A good tone in RCS sounds like a clear message from the company, without an advertising headline in every sentence. Say what has happened and what the customer can do.

paragraphs: “Your order has been shipped, with a tracking link” is often better than a long introduction about exciting news. Use names and words the customer recognizes.
The buttons need the same care. “Request rebooking” is more honest than “Rebooked” if the choice only starts a request. Read the text aloud and remove jokes that get in the way of the matter at hand.

sections.title: Be concrete even when something goes wrong
paragraphs: A service message does not have to sound stiff, but friendliness should not hide the information. If a delivery is delayed, a clear new time is better than a playful line about patience. Avoid calling a request done while it is still pending. The same principle applies to buttons, automatic replies and messages from staff: the customer should understand what has actually happened.

articles.title: What do Basic, Single and Conversation mean?
articles.description: Basic, Single and Conversation are message types in business RCS, and they are not subscription plans. They describe different kinds of content and dialogue.

paragraphs: Basic is used for simpler text messages. Single can be a rich message with media or cards. Conversation is aimed at a dialogue in which the customer and the company exchange messages.
The provider's definitions determine limits, time windows and billing. Ask for those terms before you calculate the cost of a flow; a visible reply button alone does not decide how it is billed.

sections.title: Start from the actual content
paragraphs: Begin by drawing the customer's flow: a short message, a rich campaign or a conversation with several steps. Then ask how the provider classifies each part. The names should not be treated as levels where the most expensive is always the best. A simple order status can do fine with text, while a product choice needs media. The billing rules have to be confirmed separately from the technical possibilities.

articles.title: What are suggested replies?
articles.description: Suggested replies are ready-made reply options that the customer can tap instead of typing. The Swedish name is föreslagna svar.

paragraphs: “Confirm” and “Request rebooking” can be two such choices. The reply can carry data that links it to the booking, so that the company's system knows which case is meant.
The system or the staff must handle the choice. A reply button does not change the booking by itself. It also differs from an action button that opens a web page.

sections.title: A choice has to mean something specific
paragraphs: Reply options should be possible to handle without guessing. “Yes” becomes unclear if the message contains several questions, while “Confirm attendance” has a specific purpose. Tie the choice to the right case and give the customer a confirmation that matches the system's actual result. If the booking cannot be changed automatically, the reply should describe a received request and should not claim a completed change.

articles.title: How do images and video work in RCS?
articles.description: RCS can send images and video separately or as part of a rich card. How it looks depends on the file, the messaging app and the recipient's support.

paragraphs: Use an image that can be understood on a small screen. Write prices and other important details as text, so that the customer gets the message even if the image loads slowly.
Check the service's file types, size limits and requirements for media URLs. Try loading and cropping on a phone, and write a separate SMS text if a fallback channel will be used.

sections.title: The media should support the message
paragraphs: Product images need to show what the customer is going to assess, while an instruction video needs to make a task easier. Important information must not depend on the customer being able to play sound or wait for a large file. Test a slow connection as well and write a readable text part. The cropping of the image and the first frame of the video affect what is actually visible before the customer chooses to open the content.

articles.title: How do I write a clear RCS message?
articles.description: A clear RCS message first answers what the matter is about. Images and buttons should help the customer move on, and they are no reason to add more content.

paragraphs: “Your booking is tomorrow at 2 pm”, followed by the place and a booking link, gives a concrete message. A general greeting with several offers makes the same task harder.
Write the button text after the action: “Open the order”, “Call us” or “Request rebooking”. Try the message on a phone and check that the fallback text can also be understood without images.

sections.title: Remove everything the choice does not need
paragraphs: Read the message as a customer who has not seen your internal plan. Can you tell which order or booking it concerns and where the button leads? Shorten introductions before you remove conditions or important times. A short message is not automatically clear. The goal is that the customer can act without having to guess or contact support for basic information.

articles.title: What do action buttons do in RCS?
articles.description: Action buttons in RCS can, for example, open a web page, call a number or show a location. They are called suggested actions and differ from ready-made replies that are sent to the company.

paragraphs: Say what the next step is. “Open the booking page” describes a link, while “Booked” can give the wrong impression if the customer has not yet chosen a time.
Support depends on the service, the format and the client. Check it before sending and follow the result where the action is completed. A click does not show that the customer has booked or bought.

sections.title: The button and the landing page belong together
paragraphs: A button to an order should open the order or a clear login that leads on to it. If it only opens the start page, the customer has to do the work again. Try the link in the phone's browser and check what happens when there is no session. The confirmation on the landing page should show that the action was completed; it is not enough that the messaging app opened the link.

articles.title: What is SMS fallback?
articles.description: SMS fallback means that SMS is used as a backup when RCS cannot be sent or delivered according to the terms of the flow. It needs to be arranged in the service or the integration.

paragraphs: Write a separate SMS version. A carousel or button cannot come along unchanged, but the order reference, the status and an ordinary link can give the same important message.
Decide when SMS may be sent and how a pending RCS message is stopped or expires. Otherwise the customer may receive both. Also ask how the fallback is billed.

sections.title: Keep the message, and let the form go
paragraphs: The fallback text should help the customer do the same important thing even when images and buttons are missing. A tracking link can replace a delivery card, but several offers may require a combined page. Test the SMS version as a message of its own. The time limit, the cost and the handling of late-delivered RCS need to be part of the same plan so that the fallback does not create more problems than it solves.

articles.title: What does delivery status mean in RCS?
articles.description: RCS status follows several steps in a send. Accepted means that the API has received the request. Delivered and read are later events when the service can report them.

paragraphs: Save the steps separately and link them to the right message. Then you can see whether an error occurred during the call or during delivery.
A read receipt proves neither understanding nor consent. If there is no read report, you cannot know for certain that the message is unread, since the app and its settings affect what is reported.

sections.title: Save both the event and the context
paragraphs: A status report becomes more useful if it has a message ID and a timestamp. Then you can tell a long wait from a quick error and see which channel was finally used. Do not present read as a legal confirmation or delivered as a completed customer case. If the follow-up requires a booking or a reply, that event needs to come from the right system.

articles.title: What should be tested before an RCS campaign?
articles.description: An RCS test needs to follow the customer's whole case: the message, the buttons, the reply and the update in the right system. A preview tests only one part.

paragraphs: Send to phones with confirmed support and use every choice. Try long texts, images and links and see which message the customer gets after replying.
Also test a recipient without support, time limits and the SMS fallback if it is included. Unsubscribing and the handling of duplicates should work before real customers receive the campaign.

sections.title: Also test what should not happen
paragraphs: Try to confirm the same booking twice, open an old link and reply after the case has been closed. Such tests show whether the flow protects the customer from double or incorrect changes. Also use phones with different text sizes and a recipient without RCS support. Not every test has to look perfect, but every deviation should give an understandable and safe result.

articles.title: What is a capability check?
articles.description: A capability check examines whether a recipient can be reached by a business agent and which RCS features are supported. In Swedish it is called kapabilitetskontroll.

paragraphs: It gives more useful information than the phone model. If a carousel is not supported, the service may need to choose simpler content or a fallback channel.
A positive answer is not a later delivery receipt. Support can also change, so follow the provider's rules for how long the result of the check may be used.

sections.title: Use the answer to choose content
paragraphs: A check can give a basis for choosing a carousel, simpler cards or another channel. Save which agent and which feature the check concerned, otherwise the result can be misleading when you change sender. Follow the service's freshness rules and check errors separately from a negative support answer. A temporary technical error should not automatically be read as meaning that the customer can never be reached with RCS.

articles.title: How is an RCS sender registered?
articles.description: The company needs a registered and approved RCS sender before public campaigns. In Google's model, an agent is created, followed by brand verification and launch.

paragraphs: Prepare the name, the logo, the contact details and an authorized representative. The profile should match the company the customer recognizes.
A created test agent is not the same as a launched sender. Ask the partner to confirm the approval for the markets you want to reach before the customer list is used.

sections.title: Prepare details that fit together
paragraphs: The brand name, the logo and the contact details should be recognizable from the company's other channels. Appoint someone who can confirm the partner's authorization and keep that person available during the process. Ask what remains after the verification and which markets the launch covers. A profile that looks finished in a tool is no proof that public messages can be sent to customers.

articles.title: What is an Agent?
articles.description: An agent is the company's sender on Google's RCS platform. It represents the brand in the messaging app and can be connected to the company's systems.

paragraphs: A web shop's order system can, for example, decide when the agent sends a delivery message. The agent needs to be registered and launched for public campaigns. It is not an AI; automation and AI are separate choices.

sections.title: The sender and the system behind it
paragraphs: The agent gives the company an identity in the messaging channel. What it sends is decided by a person, a web tool or a connected system. The same agent can therefore be used for simple messages without AI. When something goes wrong, you need to tell a problem with the sender's launch apart from a problem in the system that tries to send the message.

articles.title: What is an Agent profile?
articles.description: The agent profile is the company information shown for the RCS sender, such as the name and the logo. The customer should be able to recognize who is getting in touch.

paragraphs: Use the brand the customer meets, even if the legal company name is a different one. A filled-in profile does not mean that verification and launch are complete.

sections.title: The profile is the customer's orientation
paragraphs: The name and the logo show who the conversation concerns, while the contact details help the customer check or follow up on the message. The profile should therefore be maintained like any other public company information. If a support address stops working, it does not help that the logo is still right. Changes should be checked with the partner, since registration and approval can be affected.

articles.title: What is an API?
articles.description: An API lets one system request things from a service. In an RCS flow, the order system can use it to ask for a message when an order is shipped.

paragraphs: The API's response first shows whether the request was accepted. Delivery status comes later. Addresses, fields and authentication are in the documentation of the provider you use.

sections.title: A call is the beginning, and the end comes later
paragraphs: An API lets programs request an action without anyone filling in a web form. In RCS campaigns, the call needs to contain the recipient and the right content according to the provider's rules. The program also has to handle errors and later statuses. A connection that can only send but cannot follow up on delivery gives incomplete information for operations and customer service.

articles.title: What is Asynchronous delivery?
articles.description: Asynchronous delivery means that a message is handled after the first request. The system can get a response from the API before the customer has received the message.

paragraphs: Save the message ID so that later delivery, read or error events end up on the right case. Do not treat the first response as a confirmation of delivery.

sections.title: Why the answer comes later
paragraphs: The phone can be offline when the company sends. The service then needs to report what happened once the delivery has been settled, and the original call should not have to wait until the customer is back. The integration needs to recognize the message even for later events. It is the same principle as when an order number is used to follow a delivery long after the order was placed.

articles.title: What is brand verification?
articles.description: Brand verification is Google's check of the link between an RCS agent and the brand it represents. An authorized representative confirms the details and the partner's right to manage the sender.

paragraphs: Verification and launch are separate steps. The check is about identity and authorization, and says nothing about the quality of every future offer or link.

sections.title: What the check does not tell you
paragraphs: Verification ties the company identity to the party that is allowed to administer the sender. It does not assess whether your next campaign has the right price or whether every recipient may be contacted. The company is still responsible for content and rules. After an approved verification, launch steps can remain, so check the status before you plan a public send.

articles.title: What is a suggested action?
articles.description: A suggested action is a button that helps the customer do something, such as open a website. In RCS it is called a suggested action.

paragraphs: The button can take the customer out of the chat. Open the booking page is therefore clearer than Booked if the customer still has to choose a time. Support depends on the app and the service, and a click does not mean the task was completed.

sections.title: An action can leave the conversation
paragraphs: When the customer taps a web link, the task often continues in the browser. Login, choices or payment may still remain there. The name of the button should describe the next step and avoid promising a finished result. Also check what the recipient's app supports. An action that looks good in the preview may need a simpler fallback on other phones.

articles.title: What is a carousel?
articles.description: An RCS carousel is several message cards the customer can swipe between. It can show products or other options, with matching information on each card.

paragraphs: Let the first card explain the context. Important times or terms should not require the customer to swipe to the end. Test the cards on a phone and check recipient support.

sections.title: When several cards help
paragraphs: A carousel makes the options visible in the same message, but not everything is on screen at once. The customer has to swipe to see later cards. Put the context first and use the same kind of details on every option. If the order carries an important instruction, explain it in text as well; do not assume everyone swipes through all the content.

articles.title: What is a delivery receipt?
articles.description: A delivery receipt reports that a message has been delivered to the recipient's device, according to the service's status model. It arrives after the send has been requested.

paragraphs: An accepted API call is therefore not a delivery receipt. The receipt also does not show that the customer has read or understood the content.

sections.title: A technical step in the customer journey
paragraphs: The receipt helps you tell a message that has reached the device from one that is still waiting or has failed. It can be used for operational follow-up and channel choice. The customer may still have missed the notification or not yet opened the conversation. A completed payment or a changed booking therefore needs its own confirmation and should not be inferred from the delivery status.

articles.title: What is a read receipt?
articles.description: A read receipt is the messaging app's report of read status. It can help a company follow a send, but it does not show that the customer understood or accepted the message.

paragraphs: The app and its settings affect the reporting. A missing receipt is therefore not enough to say the message is unread. It is also not a measure of purchase or consent.

sections.title: Reading is not a business event
paragraphs: A read report says something about how the app reported the message status. It does not say why the customer opened the message or what the person did afterward. Use it as one step in your analysis and state how the metric is defined. Missing reports need to be kept apart from messages confirmed as unread. Otherwise both the read rate and comparisons between channels can give a misleading picture.

articles.title: What is MaaP?
articles.description: MaaP stands for Messaging as a Platform. It is a GSMA term for the platform support behind business communication over RCS.

paragraphs: It describes a technical part of the RCS ecosystem and is not an app the customer installs. A provider's features and prices should be stated in its own terms.

sections.title: The infrastructure is invisible in the inbox
paragraphs: The customer meets a business profile and a message, and never the platform layer behind them. MaaP describes how business communication can be supported in the ecosystem. When a provider uses the word, ask which concrete features are included: sender management, sending, incoming replies or reports. The abbreviation alone tells you nothing certain about the scope of the service or how it is charged.

articles.title: What is MMS?
articles.description: MMS stands for Multimedia Messaging Service and is a service for messages with, for example, images. MMS and RCS can appear in the same app but are different technologies.

paragraphs: An MMS image is not an RCS card with interactive choices. The operator sets terms such as media limits and costs for MMS.

sections.title: Image support is a different format
paragraphs: MMS can carry media but does not have the same structured cards and reply options as business RCS. A photo in the inbox is therefore not enough to tell which channel was used. The operator's and the phone's conditions also affect MMS. If you choose MMS as a fallback, the content needs to be tested in that format, and not just copied from a rich RCS card.

articles.title: What is an operator?
articles.description: The mobile operator provides your subscription and can affect which RCS features you can use. This shows most clearly when an iPhone needs operator support.

paragraphs: A compatible phone is not enough if the feature is missing for the subscription. For a business send, the provider also needs to confirm reach from the registered sender.

sections.title: Network and subscription are different matters
paragraphs: A mobile brand can use another company's network without every service and setting being identical. Ask the operator responsible for your subscription. For iPhone, explicit RCS support is especially relevant. For a business send, the sender's partner also needs to check that the registered agent can reach the phone number, regardless of the network's general RCS information.

articles.title: What is P2P?
articles.description: P2P means person to person. In RCS it refers to private chat, for example when two people write to each other in Google Messages.

paragraphs: Business messages from a registered agent are a different use. Information about encryption or support in private chat should therefore not be carried over to a business flow without checking.

sections.title: A private conversation, different conditions
paragraphs: P2P describes the participants and is not a campaign feature. Two people can chat in their messaging apps without the agent registration that business RCS uses. Information about read receipts or encryption needs to be read in that context. A test between colleagues' phones is useful for private chat but does not show whether the company's upcoming sender is launched or reaches the same numbers.

articles.title: What is postback data?
articles.description: Postback data is information that comes along when the customer picks a reply or an action. The company's systems can use it to understand which choice was made.

paragraphs: A button can show Confirm while the data identifies the booking. Use a stable identifier instead of interpreting the button text. The system must then handle the choice; the data itself changes no booking.

sections.title: Let the system read a stable choice
paragraphs: The text on a button can change between languages or campaigns. The data behind the choice, on the other hand, should identify the same action and the right case. Tie it to a reference and check that the case can still be changed when the reply arrives. An old button press should not be able to confirm a booking that has already been canceled or belongs to another customer.

articles.title: What is RBM?
articles.description: RBM stands for RCS Business Messaging, the business use of RCS. A company can send content under a registered sender and receive customer replies.
keywords: rcs business messaging rcs for business

paragraphs: In Google's model the sender is called an agent. It needs to be verified and launched, and the service must be able to reach the recipients. A working private RCS conversation is not enough as a test of such a send.

sections.title: The business side of RCS
paragraphs: RBM covers more than putting an image in a private message. The company uses a registered identity and needs to handle sending, customer replies and statuses through a service. How this is offered varies between providers. Ask for concrete information about launch, reach and what happens when a recipient cannot be reached, rather than judging the service by the abbreviation.

articles.title: What is RCS chat?
articles.description: An RCS chat is a conversation that uses RCS over wifi or mobile data. Where it is supported, participants can share images, see read receipts and see when someone is typing.

paragraphs: Both sides need support and a connection. The same app can use SMS or MMS in another conversation, or as a fallback when the settings allow it. Read the channel label to see what is being used.

sections.title: The same inbox can switch channel
paragraphs: It is the channel of the message, and not the name of the contact, that decides which features are available. A conversation can use RCS when the conditions are right and SMS or MMS in another situation. Check what the text field shows before you send. The fact that older messages in the thread had read receipts does not mean the next message is sent the same way.

articles.title: What is an RCS client?
articles.description: An RCS client is the app that handles RCS on the phone. Google Messages and Apple's Messages are examples of apps that can use the technology.

paragraphs: The client's version and settings affect the features, together with the operator. The same content therefore needs to be tried in the apps your customers use.

sections.title: The app shapes the experience
paragraphs: The client decides how text, media and choices are presented on screen, within the support that exists. Updates, text size and settings can therefore change the experience even when the sender sends the same content. For companies this means a preview needs to be complemented with phone tests. Important messages should be understandable even when an image is cropped or a button appears in a different place.

articles.title: What is a rich card?
articles.description: A rich card is a structured RCS card with room for media, a title, a description and choices. It can, for example, present a product with an image and a link.

paragraphs: In Google's model the card needs to contain media, a title or a description; not all parts have to be present at the same time. Put necessary details in text and test the format on the recipient devices.

sections.title: Keep what belongs together
paragraphs: The card is a content format and is not a web page of its own. It fits when an image and a short text explain the same product, time or message. Let the button take the customer on to a relevant action and write the essentials so that the image does not carry the information alone. If several cards are needed, a carousel can be used, but more parts do not automatically make the message clearer.

articles.title: What is a typing indicator?
articles.description: A typing indicator shows that the other person is writing in an RCS chat. It says nothing about which reply is coming or whether anything is sent.

paragraphs: Google describes the feature for private chats. If a business flow is going to use it, you need to check support for that service.

sections.title: Presence without a promise of a reply
paragraphs: The indicator can help participants see that someone is active, but what is being written can change or never be sent. It should therefore not be used as a basis for closing a case or assuming the customer has accepted something. In a business flow, real incoming replies need to be handled separately. Staffing and the promised response time should also be stated independently of the indicator.

articles.title: What is SMS?
articles.description: SMS stands for Short Message Service and is the service for ordinary text messages over the mobile network. It does not need an active internet connection.

paragraphs: A single SMS normally holds 160 GSM-7 characters. Other characters and longer text can produce more parts. SMS does not have RCS cards or their built-in buttons, and a delivery report is not a read receipt.

sections.title: A simple fallback needs its own content
paragraphs: SMS is useful for a short message when the content does not need a rich format. An ordinary web link can lead onward, but it is not the same thing as a built-in RCS action. Check the encoding and length of the text before you calculate the cost. If SMS is used as a fallback, the customer should still be able to understand the matter without having seen the RCS version.

articles.title: What is a webhook?
articles.description: A webhook is an HTTPS address that receives events from a service. In RCS it can be a delivery status or a customer reply that needs to be passed on to your system.

paragraphs: Tie the event to the message ID and the right case. Also verify where the call comes from, following the provider's documentation, before it is allowed to change anything. Valid JSON does not prove that the sender is trusted.

sections.title: Events have to be handled
paragraphs: The webhook is the receiving address, while the business rules live in the system behind it. An incoming reply can, for example, be registered first and then sent to the right queue or order. Plan what happens if processing fails after receipt. Redeliveries need to be recognizable so that a temporary disruption does not lead to several confirmations or duplicate changes.

articles.title: Which Swedish operators support RCS?
articles.description: Tele2 and Comviq state that RCS works on both iPhone and Android. For other Swedish operators, you need to ask about support for your subscription and your phone.

paragraphs: Apple's operator list and the operators' own support pages do not give the same answer: on November 1, 2026, the Sweden section at Apple had no RCS markings, despite Tele2's and Comviq's statements about iPhone support. It is therefore not possible to give a certain answer for the whole of Sweden from that list.

If a company is going to send RCS, a different check is needed. The provider must be able to reach the customers from the company's registered sender. The fact that two people can chat over RCS does not tell you whether a business send reaches the same phones.

sections.title: Build a useful picture of support
paragraphs: Split the question into private Android chat, private iPhone chat and business messages. The three answers can differ for the same customer. When a support statement is unclear, note the source and which phone or line the answer applies to. For planned sends, a test from the registered sender to a relevant recipient sample is more useful than adding up the operators' general launch news.

articles.title: Does RCS work with Tele2?
articles.description: Yes, according to Tele2's support. It states iOS 18 or later for iPhone and Android 5.0 or later with Google Messages for Android.

paragraphs: You and the person you are writing to both need to have RCS turned on and be connected. Look at the conversation's text field to see whether it uses RCS. The phone's main setting only tells you that the feature is switched on.

If the option is missing on an updated phone, ask Tele2 about your specific subscription. The answer here applies to private chat and is based on the support page on November 1, 2026. Business sends need to be checked with the sending provider.

sections.title: When a subscription needs to be checked
paragraphs: If support is described but does not show up on the phone, the troubleshooting needs to be more specific. State the model, the system version and whether the problem concerns one particular conversation or the RCS setting itself. A test between two phones can show where the difference lies. Avoid drawing conclusions about all Tele2 customers from a single test, especially when business messages are the real use case.

articles.title: Does RCS work with Comviq?
articles.description: Comviq says RCS works on iPhone and Android. Its support states iOS 18 or later for iPhone and Google Messages on a compatible Android phone.

paragraphs: On Android you can see the connection status under RCS chats in the app's settings. On iPhone you can see which channel a conversation uses in the text field. The person you are writing to also needs RCS and internet.

The information comes from Comviq's support page on November 1, 2026. If you wonder about prepaid cards or the setting is missing, ask Comviq to check your number. Support at another operator does not answer that question.

sections.title: Test your number and not the network's reputation
paragraphs: Comviq's own information is the relevant starting point even when the same network is used by other brands. If you have changed SIM or phone, the number registration may need to be checked before the problem is put down to operator support. First see which status the app shows. For companies, a successful private test should be followed by a check from the actual business sender to the same recipient.

articles.title: How do I check RCS with Telia?
articles.description: Ask Telia about RCS for your phone and your subscription. Apple's Swedish carrier list had no RCS marking for Telia on November 1, 2026, so it gives no confirmed yes.

paragraphs: The absence from the list is not enough for a certain no either, especially for Android. There you can open Google Messages yourself and read the status under RCS chats. On iPhone, your subscription needs carrier support.
Say which phone you have when you ask Telia. An answer about the company's bulk messaging service is not an answer about private RCS on your mobile number.

sections.title: Ask a question that can be answered
paragraphs: Ask for an answer for your subscription, phone model and system version, and say explicitly that you mean private RCS in the messaging app. Ask what you should see in the settings if it is activated. If the answer concerns another service or market, your question has not been answered. A missing marking in an external list should not replace a current answer about your line.

articles.title: How do I check RCS with Telenor?
articles.description: Ask Telenor to confirm RCS for your subscription and say whether you use iPhone or Android. Apple's Swedish Telenor section had no RCS marking when checked on November 1, 2026.

paragraphs: On Android you can get a more concrete answer from the connection status in Google Messages. On iPhone, both the iOS version and the subscription's support need to be in place. An updated phone does not fix missing carrier support.
If Telenor describes a service for business messaging, that is a different use. Ask for an explicit answer about private chat for your line.

sections.title: Tell carrier support from a local fault
paragraphs: If the carrier confirms support, the next check can be the app's status and which line the phone uses. If support is not confirmed, it does not help to keep switching the same setting. Ask whether the answer applies to iPhone, Android or both. That reduces the risk that a general statement about RCS is misread as support on a specific phone.

articles.title: How do I check RCS with Tre?
articles.description: Tre needs to confirm whether RCS works on your subscription. When checked on November 1, 2026, Apple did not list RCS in its Swedish section for 3.

paragraphs: That does not say everything about Android, where the RCS status in Google Messages can show whether the connection works. For iPhone, Tre should confirm support for the line you use.

Have your phone model and system version ready when you contact support. Also say whether you have a SIM or an eSIM. Start there rather than resetting the phone for a feature that may not be activated by the carrier.

sections.title: Save the conditions of the test
paragraphs: Note which phone and subscription were tested and which channel the text field shows. That makes the result comparable with the carrier's answer without mixing up different lines. A successful Android conversation says nothing on its own about iPhone. If your goal is business messaging, the agent and content type should also be part of the test description.

articles.title: Can I assume RCS support from the carrier's network?
articles.description: You cannot assume that Hallon, Fello, Vimla or Halebop have the same RCS support as the carrier whose network they use. Network coverage and messaging features are separate things.
keywords: rcs hallon fello vimla halebop network

paragraphs: Ask your own brand about your subscription and specify iPhone or Android. Features may need to be activated separately even when two subscriptions use the same mobile network.
Then try with a contact who has working RCS and read the channel text in the app. An unclear support answer should be recorded as unconfirmed support and not turned into a yes.

sections.title: The same network does not mean the same service
paragraphs: The name of the carrier on the subscription matters more than which network a coverage map shows. Terms of service and activation can differ between brands. Ask specifically about iPhone support and the subscription you use. On Android, the app's connection status can give a concrete test, but a positive private test still does not answer the question of reach from a registered business agent.

articles.title: Why do Apple's and the carrier's RCS statements differ?
articles.description: Tele2 and Comviq confirmed iPhone support on their support pages on November 1, 2026. The same day, Apple's Swedish carrier list had no RCS markings. The pages gave different answers.

paragraphs: We do not know why the information differs. It would therefore be wrong to pick an explanation, for example that one page is out of date, without evidence.

If you want to chat, an answer about your subscription and a test in the app are the most useful. For business messaging, the provider must also confirm which customers the registered sender can reach.

sections.title: Report the difference instead of guessing
paragraphs: Two support pages may describe different scopes or may have been updated at different times. Save the exact wording and the date of the check before you compare them. If one page is about iPhone and the other about RCS in general, the statements are not directly comparable. When uncertainty remains, the article should say what is confirmed and refer the subscription question to the carrier.

articles.title: What happens to RCS when I switch carriers?
articles.description: When you switch carriers, RCS may need to be checked again, even if you keep your number. The new carrier may have different conditions, especially for iPhone.

paragraphs: When the number transfer is done, check that the right number is used in the messaging app and read the RCS status. Try with someone who already has working RCS.
If it stopped working at the switch, tell support, together with the date of the number transfer. That helps them tell registration problems from problems in a single chat.

sections.title: Let the new line be the starting point
paragraphs: After a carrier switch, the phone number can stay the same while the subscription's services have changed. Check the RCS status on the new line and try a new conversation once the switch is complete. Old messages show how the service worked earlier, not what is active now. If the registration is stuck, support needs to know when the switch happened and which status the app shows.

articles.title: Why did RCS stop working after a SIM swap?
articles.description: After a SIM or eSIM swap, the app's number registration or choice of line may need to be reviewed. First check that the right number is active and that the internet works.
keywords: rcs new sim esim not working

paragraphs: Then read the RCS status in the messaging app. On Android it is in Google Messages. On iPhone you also need to confirm that RCS is available for the new line.
If the problem remains, tell support when the SIM card was swapped and what the app shows. That is better information than just reporting that messages do not arrive.
