sections.title: Check which number is being registered
paragraphs: A new SIM can affect which line the app tries to use even if the phone is the same. Look at the number in the RCS settings and at whether regular calls and SMS work after the swap. If the registration does not complete, follow the app's official help instead of making many changes at once. That also makes it easier to describe the problem to support.

articles.title: Which number does RCS use with dual SIM?
articles.description: With dual SIM, RCS may use a different number than you intended. Check which line the conversation and the messaging app are set to.

paragraphs: The phone's line for mobile data and the number registered for RCS do not have to be the same. How they are chosen differs between apps and phones.
Test one line at a time with a known RCS contact. If the number in the settings is wrong, take it up with the carrier or the app's support. Support on one line does not confirm support on the other.

sections.title: Test one line at a time
paragraphs: When the phone has two subscriptions, you need to know which number the current conversation uses. The default line for mobile data is not in itself proof of which RCS identity is used. Support for dual lines depends on the app and version. Document each line's status and try a conversation with a known RCS number before you interpret the result as a carrier problem.

articles.title: Why is the RCS setting missing on iPhone?
articles.description: The RCS option can be missing on iPhone when the carrier or subscription does not support the feature. Apple requires both a compatible iOS version and carrier support.

paragraphs: Update the phone and ask the carrier about your number. The fact that a friend has RCS on the same iPhone model does not mean your subscription has the same support.
If the carrier confirms that it should work, give your phone model, iOS version and which line is active. Then support can look into why the option is still missing.

sections.title: A missing option and a turned-off option are different
paragraphs: If the setting does not exist, the first question is whether the carrier offers the feature for the line, rather than how to turn it on. Also check the system version and which line is selected. If the option exists but the conversation goes as SMS, the recipient's support also needs to be examined. That distinction helps support choose the right troubleshooting and avoid unnecessary resets.

articles.title: What do I do when RCS gets stuck on verifying?
articles.description: When RCS stays on verifying, the number registration is not complete. First check that the app shows the right number and that the phone has internet.

paragraphs: Update Google Messages and follow Google's troubleshooting advice. Switching the toggle off and on over and over is not a reliable shortcut.
Write down the status message if you need help. Say whether you have recently changed phone, number, SIM or carrier; that can make it easier to find the cause.

sections.title: Make the troubleshooting traceable
paragraphs: Write down the status that is actually shown and check which number the app is trying to register. If you have recently moved the number or changed devices, that is important information. Make one change at a time following Google's help so that the result can be understood. A verification problem is not the same thing as a particular contact lacking support, and the two problems should be troubleshot differently.

articles.title: Why does RCS only work with some contacts?
articles.description: A phone can use RCS with one contact and SMS with another. Both participants must have working RCS in that specific conversation.
keywords: rcs only works with some contacts

paragraphs: Ask the contact to check that RCS is on and the internet works. Also make sure you are writing to the right number, especially if the person has recently changed it.

Try a simple text to someone who usually works with RCS. If it goes through, your own connection is probably not the whole problem. Then keep troubleshooting the contact or chat where the problem occurs.

sections.title: Compare two conversations, not the whole phone
paragraphs: When one conversation works with RCS and another does not, you already have a sign that your own connection may work. Ask the other contact which app and status they have, and check the channel text in both conversations. A missing read receipt is not proof of SMS on its own, because the reporting can be affected by settings.

articles.title: How can I see whether a message is sent as RCS?
articles.description: Read the channel text in the conversation's text field or the message details. The bubble color is not enough: on iPhone, RCS is green, just like SMS and MMS.

paragraphs: Tele2 describes that the text field shows RCS message when the channel is used. On Android, the app's channel marking and connection status can give similar guidance.
For a message that has been resent, you need to read its own status. A working RCS connection right now does not tell you how an earlier message was sent.

sections.title: Look before and after sending
paragraphs: The text field can show which channel the app intends to use. After sending, the message details can give further information, depending on the app. Images and green bubbles are less reliable clues because other channels can show them too. For troubleshooting, it is good to note the exact channel text instead of describing the message as a regular SMS or a picture message.

articles.title: Does a green bubble mean it is SMS?
articles.description: A green bubble on iPhone can be RCS, SMS or MMS. Blue bubbles are iMessage. Green therefore does not automatically mean SMS.

paragraphs: Look at the channel text in the text field for a better answer. Read receipts and better image sharing can occur with RCS, but they also depend on settings and the recipient's support.
When troubleshooting, write down what the app says about the channel. The color alone gives support too little information to tell an SMS fault from an RCS fault.

sections.title: The color only tells part of the story
paragraphs: A green thread can carry RCS in one conversation and SMS or MMS in another. The color should therefore not be used as an availability check or as proof that RCS has stopped working. Read the channel text and check the recipient's support. If you are helping someone else troubleshoot, a description of that text is more useful than the bubble color alone.

articles.title: Does RCS work when I am abroad?
articles.description: RCS can work abroad over wifi or mobile data. The app still needs to be connected, and both your subscription and the recipient must have support.

paragraphs: Ask the carrier about data roaming and the terms for the country you are visiting. Wifi can provide internet without mobile data, but the charges for any fallback SMS are a separate question.
Try it before you need to send an important message. If the app chooses SMS or MMS, different prices may apply than for your regular data use.

sections.title: Keep connectivity and charges apart
paragraphs: Wifi can give an internet connection without you using mobile roaming data, but the service's other conditions still need to be met. With mobile data, the cost depends on the subscription and the country. Check both the data terms and the RCS status. If the app uses SMS as a fallback, other charges may apply; a successful RCS test at home is not a price quote for a trip abroad.

articles.title: Does RCS work with a prepaid SIM?
articles.description: RCS on a prepaid SIM needs to be confirmed by the carrier for that specific card. An answer about the carrier's subscriptions does not necessarily cover all prepaid cards.

paragraphs: You need internet and a working registration in the app. For iPhone, the carrier's answer should also apply to iPhone, not only Android.
Check the price for SMS and MMS if the app uses them as a fallback. An RCS message over wifi and a fallback SMS can draw on different parts of the prepaid balance.

sections.title: Ask for an answer for the prepaid SIM
paragraphs: A general carrier answer may refer to other subscriptions than yours. Check that the number is active and ask about RCS for the prepaid SIM and the phone specifically. RCS uses the internet, so access to wifi or data also matters. Keep any SMS charges separate from data usage, especially if the app can use another channel when RCS does not work.

articles.title: What do I need to do with RCS when I change phones?
articles.description: When you move your number to a new phone, check that RCS uses the right number there. The app should show that the connection works before you rely on it.

paragraphs: Follow the app's advice on turning off or deregistering RCS on the old device, especially if you are changing messaging app. Then review the settings on the new one.
Test both RCS and regular SMS. If something stopped working at the move, give support the model and app for both phones so that they can trace what changed.

sections.title: History and connection do not move the same way
paragraphs: The fact that old messages appear on the new phone does not mean RCS is connected there. Check the number and the app's status, and follow the official transfer help if the old device is still linked. Then send a new test to a contact with support. Judge the new delivery, not just how earlier RCS messages are displayed after the transfer.

articles.title: How do I turn off RCS?
articles.description: On iPhone you turn off RCS under Settings, Apps, Messages and RCS Messaging. On Android the toggle is in Google Messages' settings for RCS chats.

paragraphs: If you no longer have the Android phone, use Google's help for deregistration. Just deleting the app is not the same as turning off the registration.
After turning it off, the app may use SMS or MMS where possible. They have their own charges and network requirements. Check separately whether older pending messages have arrived.

sections.title: What turning it off does not do
paragraphs: Turning off RCS changes how future messages can be sent, but it does not take back messages that have already reached someone else. SMS and MMS can still be used when their conditions are met. If you change app or leave an old phone, you should follow the service's instructions for the number so that messages do not keep being linked to a registration you no longer use.

articles.title: Can I turn off business RCS on iPhone?
articles.description: Apple describes a separate toggle for RCS business messages. It is under Settings, Apps, Messages and RCS Messaging when the feature is available.
keywords: turn off rcs business messages iphone

paragraphs: With it you can turn off business messages without turning off private RCS chat. If the option is missing, check the software and what the carrier supports.

If you want to stop receiving advertising from a particular company, you should also unsubscribe with the company. A channel toggle in the phone does not reliably change your choices for email or other mailings.

sections.title: Separate businesses from private contacts
paragraphs: Apple describes a separate option for business messages where the feature is available. Read what the option affects before you use the broader setting for all RCS. Stopping business RCS in the phone is not necessarily the same as unsubscribing from a company's advertising list in other channels. If you want to stop all marketing, the company also needs to get that message.

articles.title: How do I block a business in Google Messages?
articles.description: Open the business chat in Google Messages and use the app's options for blocking, reporting or unsubscribing. Which options you see can vary.

paragraphs: Read what the option does. Reporting spam to the app and asking the company to stop sending can be different actions.
You can also contact the company to object to its direct marketing. Save the confirmation if you want to be able to follow up that the mailings have stopped.

sections.title: Blocking and unsubscribing have different reach
paragraphs: Blocking in the app can help against further messages there, while an objection to the company may be needed for advertising in other channels. Check what the app states when you block or report. If a message looks fraudulent, you should not open its link to find help. Use the company's known website or a contact route you found independently of the message.

articles.title: What happens in a group chat if someone lacks RCS?
articles.description: A group where someone lacks RCS may get different features than an RCS group. What works depends on which channels the participants' apps can use together.

paragraphs: Read the channel text for the group. Image quality, read receipts and handling of participants can change when another channel is used.

Test with the people who will actually be in it. A working conversation between two people does not tell you how the whole group works. A private group chat is also something different from a business mailing.

sections.title: The group needs to be judged as a whole
paragraphs: The features in a group can differ from a single conversation because every participant's conditions matter. Check what the app shows for the group in question before you count on read receipts or media sharing. If a participant changes phone, the situation can change. A private test in a group is also not a model for how a registered business agent sends to a customer list.

articles.title: What should I include when I ask for help with RCS?
articles.description: Support needs to know what is happening, when it started and which app you use. Add your phone model, system version, carrier and the RCS status you see.

paragraphs: Say whether the problem affects one contact or all of them, and whether you recently changed SIM card, phone or number. Also check whether the internet works and which channel the chat is using.
Do not send passwords or one-time codes. If you need a screenshot, hide private conversations and any personal data that the troubleshooting does not require.

sections.title: Give support one specific incident
paragraphs: Describe when the problem happened, what you were trying to do and which status or channel text was shown. A single concrete example is easier to follow than a general statement that RCS sometimes feels broken. Separate a failed registration attempt from a problem with one contact. Do not share entire private conversations unnecessarily; choose the details needed to understand the connection, the device and the subscription.

articles.title: How do you verify the sender of an RCS webhook?
articles.description: An RCS webhook must check who is sending the request before it processes the event. Valid JSON or a known message ID does not prove that the request is genuine.

paragraphs: Use the verification method in your provider's documentation. Google's method applies to Google's platform; another provider may require a different check.
A rejected request must not change a booking or mark an order as delivered. Log the failure so it can be investigated, but keep secrets and unnecessary customer details out of the log.

sections.title: Verify before anything changes
paragraphs: A request can contain well-formed data and still come from the wrong sender. Verification therefore needs to happen before customer cases or delivery statuses are updated. Follow the method your provider documents, and plan for rotating keys or other verification credentials as well. Log that the check failed without exposing secrets or full customer messages in the troubleshooting material.

articles.title: How do I handle duplicate RCS events?
articles.description: The same webhook event may be received more than once without the customer's case changing several times. This is usually called idempotent handling.

paragraphs: Store the event's identifier and check whether it has already been processed. A repeated cancellation reply, for example, must not start a new cancellation or refund.
The receiving end can acknowledge a duplicate without repeating the action. Keep apart the fact that the event was received and the fact that a change was made in the booking system.

sections.title: Make processing safe to repeat
paragraphs: If the same delivery event arrives twice, the result should normally be one delivery status, not two new customer activities. Store a stable identifier for the event or for the action you are processing. The same principle applies to customer replies that change a booking. Also check for concurrency: two copies arriving close together must not both carry out the change before either has been marked as done.

articles.title: What do I do if a webhook is delivered again?
articles.description: If a webhook is delivered again, your system should be able to receive it without performing the same action a second time. Your provider's documentation sets the terms for redelivery.

paragraphs: Verify and store the event before slow processing starts. That makes it possible to tell a failed receipt from an error in the customer system.
Test by sending the same event several times. A customer should get one correctly updated order, not several orders or messages for the same choice.

sections.title: Receiving and business processing can be separated
paragraphs: The service needs to get the right response to the webhook request according to its rules, while heavier processing can continue in your system. If an external order service is slow, that should not automatically cause several identical order changes. Decide what is stored on receipt and what can be retried later. Also monitor events that get stuck, so that a technically accepted response does not hide an unprocessed customer case.

articles.title: Do RCS events have to arrive in the right order?
articles.description: Plan for an event arriving later than it happened. The time your system receives an event does not have to match the time the message event occurred.

paragraphs: Use the provider's documented time fields and link each event to the right message. A late delivery report, for example, must not overwrite a later read report.
Decide which status changes are allowed. Then the system can handle both late reports and duplicates without the customer case moving backward by mistake.

sections.title: Let the status model tolerate late reports
paragraphs: If an older delivery report is processed after a read report, it must not mark the message as unread again. Store the events' own timestamps and define which transitions are allowed. It is also a good idea to keep the history for troubleshooting instead of only overwriting the latest value. For business events, such as a rebooking, you also need to check the current state of the case before anything is changed.

articles.title: Why put RCS events in a queue?
articles.description: A queue lets the webhook receive events quickly while the order or support system works at its own pace. It can be useful when processing takes time.

paragraphs: A queue is one way to build the integration, and RCS does not require it. It needs protection against lost events and events processed twice.
Make sure you can find what is waiting, what is finished and what has failed. A webhook acknowledgment says that the event was received, and does not say that the customer's case is done.

sections.title: A queue only helps if you follow it up
paragraphs: A queue can separate fast receipt from work that takes longer and leave room for retries. Still, an accepted message can get stuck in the queue. Follow queue age and failed processing, and do not look only at the number of requests received. The customer's question needs to reach the right staff or system even when one of the steps has had a temporary disruption.

articles.title: How do I link RCS to the right customer case?
articles.description: Store which message ID belongs to which order, booking or support question. When replies and statuses come back, the system can then find the right case.

paragraphs: The phone number is not always enough. The same customer can have several orders and receive several messages on the same day. Visible button text is also too unspecific for that link.
Send only the data that is needed in a button choice. A case ID can often replace a whole set of customer and order details.

sections.title: Keep the link all the way through
paragraphs: Tie the message ID to the internal order or case when the send is created. The phone number is not enough because the same customer can have several active orders. When a status or a reply comes back, you can then find the right context. Avoid putting sensitive customer details directly in the identifier; use a reference that only authorized systems can look up.

articles.title: What should an RCS integration log?
articles.description: A useful log shows the message identifier, timestamps and status from the request to later events. The full message text does not need to be copied into every log.

paragraphs: API keys must never end up there. Also limit customer replies and other personal data to what the troubleshooting needs, with the right access and retention period.
Log receipt and processing separately. Then you can see whether a missing order update is because the event never arrived or because the customer system could not process it.

sections.title: Log so that an error can be followed
paragraphs: A useful log shows the time, the message reference, which step ran and the result. It does not need to contain the full message text or the customer's files. Separate errors in the send request from errors in the reporting back. With a connected reference, support can follow a case without broader log access giving access to unnecessary personal data at the same time.

articles.title: How do I protect API keys for RCS?
articles.description: A secret API key should live in a protected server environment. Do not put it in the code of a web page, a public document or a support screenshot.

paragraphs: Limit the key's access where the provider offers it. Decide who can replace it and how you will act if you suspect a leak.
Keep test and production separate when the service allows it. Also try a key rotation in advance, so that a necessary change does not become an uncontrolled outage.

sections.title: Limit both use and exposure
paragraphs: A secret key must not be sent to the customer's browser or sit in a public code example. Give the integration the access it needs and keep test and production separate where the service allows it. Plan how an exposed key is blocked and replaced without losing operational control. Troubleshooting logs should show that authentication failed, and should never print the secret itself.

articles.title: What happens if the RCS request is invalid?
articles.description: An invalid RCS request can be rejected before any delivery begins. The error code shows whether the problem concerns, for example, format, permissions or content.

paragraphs: Read the response before you try again. An incorrect field needs to be corrected; sending the same request more times does not make it valid.
Separate this from a message that was accepted but later cannot be delivered. The two cases arise at different steps and need different troubleshooting.

sections.title: Retries need a reason
paragraphs: A request with the wrong recipient format or invalid content does not become correct just because it is sent again. Read the error type and fix the root cause. Temporary errors may need different handling, but even then the same message needs to be recognized. If the response disappears after a request, the integration must be able to check the state without automatically creating a duplicate customer message.

articles.title: How should phone numbers be entered in RCS requests?
articles.description: Follow the API's requirements for number format. International format with a country code is common, but your provider's documentation decides the details.
keywords: RCS phone number format country code

paragraphs: Check imported numbers before sending, especially when Swedish local numbers need a country code. A correctly formatted number can still be the wrong number or lack RCS support.
Do not guess when the data is unclear. It could send customer information to the wrong person. Keep the original number where needed so that an uncertain normalization can be sorted out.

sections.title: Normalize before the send is created
paragraphs: A number from a spreadsheet can contain spaces, a local format or a missing country code. Do not pass it on as a guess in the send request; check and normalize it according to the service's documentation. A technically valid number still says nothing about contact rules or RCS support. They need to be checked separately, so that the number check does not become an unwarranted approval of the recipient list.

articles.title: Why does an RCS message need a validity period?
articles.description: A booking reminder that arrives after the visit helps nobody. A validity period sets a limit on how long a time-sensitive RCS message may keep trying to be delivered.

paragraphs: Check how the service specifies the time and what happens when it runs out. A separate decision about an SMS fallback may be needed.
Let the limit follow the case. A reminder and an offer may need different times, and a fallback SMS should not keep spreading the same message after it has become out of date.

sections.title: Timeliness belongs to the case
paragraphs: A reminder and a general delivery notice may need different time limits. Start from when the customer can still use the information, and do not rely on a convenient default setting. Once the message has expired, any retries and fallback channels also need to respect the limit. Otherwise a technically successful delivery can give wrong advice, for example to come to an appointment time that has already passed.

articles.title: Can I stop a pending RCS message?
articles.description: Some services can stop or revoke pending RCS messages. Whether it is possible depends on the service and on the message's status. Do not assume that a message that has already been delivered can be deleted on the customer's phone.

paragraphs: Check the message ID, the status and the response to the stop attempt. Only a confirmation shows that the stop succeeded.
If a fallback SMS is to be sent afterward, the stop needs to be part of the same decision. An unconfirmed cancellation can otherwise be followed by both an SMS and a late RCS message.

sections.title: Check what was actually stopped
paragraphs: A request to stop a pending message needs to be followed by the response or status that the service documents. The message may already have moved on or been delivered. Separate a requested cancellation from a confirmed cancellation. If the aim is to send an SMS instead, that difference needs to be part of the fallback logic so that the customer does not receive the same message through two channels.

articles.title: How do I avoid sending both RCS and SMS to the same customer?
articles.description: A customer can receive both an SMS and an RCS message if a fallback SMS is sent while the RCS version is still waiting for delivery. Plan the two channels as one shared flow.
keywords: RCS SMS duplicate messages fallback timing

paragraphs: Use status, validity period and any revocation according to your service's documentation. Decide when the SMS may be sent and how a late RCS message should be handled.
Test with delayed delivery, and do not test only a direct failure. That test can reveal a double delivery that goes unnoticed when each channel is tested on its own.

sections.title: Coordinate the channel decisions
paragraphs: The decision to send an SMS and the follow-up of the pending RCS message should belong to the same case. If different systems make decisions independently of each other, both may think they need to send. Record which channel was chosen and how later statuses are handled. Test in particular the case where the RCS report arrives just as the fallback starts; that is where a simple timing rule is often insufficient.

articles.title: Can customers send files to a business via RCS?
articles.description: Customers can send files in the incoming message types that Google's RCS for Business supports. Your service and your customer system also need to be able to receive and handle them.

paragraphs: Find out which file types are passed on. Attachments are external content and need suitable security checks and limited access.
If a file cannot be used, tell the customer and offer a secure alternative route. A case should not sit idle because an attachment could not be opened.

sections.title: Do not accept more than you can handle
paragraphs: A customer can send a photo or document that contains more information than the case needs. Check the file type and handle the content with suitable protection before staff open it. Decide where the file is stored and for how long. If the service cannot process the format, the customer should get an understandable message and a working alternative route, and a silent failure is not enough.

articles.title: How do I handle an unexpected customer reply in RCS?
articles.description: Customers can type freely even when you have planned for reply buttons. The integration's reply handling therefore needs to cover more than the preset options.
keywords: RCS free text unexpected reply bot

paragraphs: If the text is unclear, ask for clarification or hand over to staff. A guess must never become an order or a cancellation.
Keep the link to the conversation when someone takes over. Then staff can see what the customer has tried to do, instead of asking the same questions again.

sections.title: Free text is part of reality
paragraphs: The customer may write something other than what you prepared on the buttons, or reply to an older message. The flow therefore needs to recognize context without assuming that every text is a valid order change. Ask for clarification when needed and pass the conversation to staff when in doubt. An automatic standard reply is not enough if the customer is actually describing a new problem.

articles.title: How does a business handle a shared location in RCS?
articles.description: Google's business model can receive a location from the customer. To use it, you need to link the location to the right conversation and know what it is going to be used for.

paragraphs: A map position is not always a delivery address. Ask the customer to confirm the address when the case requires it. Sharing a location is also no consent to continued tracking.
Limit access and storage. If the system cannot handle the location, explain that and ask the customer to type the address that is needed.

sections.title: The location needs a purpose
paragraphs: A shared location can help with a delivery or service case, but it should not automatically be copied to all customer systems. Check which case it concerns and who needs the information. Also confirm whether the location is sufficient for the task or whether an address is still required. Avoid describing a received location as a finished booking or a confirmed delivery point until it has been checked.

articles.title: Do different brands need different RCS senders?
articles.description: Several brands may need different RCS senders if customers recognize them as separate companies. Start from the identity the customer meets, and do not base it only on your internal organization.

paragraphs: One agent per department is not a general requirement. Support and delivery can belong to the same brand even if different teams work on them.
Check the structure before registration. The approval for a sender applies to the registered identity and should not be treated as an approval for all of the group's names.

sections.title: Start from what the customer recognizes
paragraphs: If the customer shops from two different brands, a shared, unfamiliar sender can make the messages harder to understand. Discuss profile and registration with your partner based on the actual customer contact. At the same time, internal systems need to be able to link each send to the right business. More agents do not automatically give a better structure if replies and contact details still end up in the wrong place.

articles.title: What information is needed before an RCS launch?
articles.description: Before a launch, the company needs to describe who the sender is, how the messages are used and how customers can reply or unsubscribe. Google describes such information in its launch material.

paragraphs: Show the real flow. An image of a card does not say how a customer ends up in the send or how a reply is handled.
Ask your partner for the requirements for your market. That the material has been submitted does not mean the sender is approved to start sending.

sections.title: Make the approval possible to complete
paragraphs: The information must be consistent across the profile, the website and the authorized representative. If different names or old contact routes are used, the process may need explanations. Ask your partner to make clear which parts remain and which markets the application covers. Do not plan the date of the customer send solely on the form having been filled in; the actual launch status needs to be settled.

articles.title: What is the difference between a test agent and a launched sender?
articles.description: A test agent is used to try out content and integration with permitted test recipients. A launched sender has also passed the platform's approval for public sends.

paragraphs: Check which mode the sender is in before you use the customer list. A created agent may still be waiting for verification or launch.
Keep test numbers and real recipients separate. A successful demo confirms the test, and says nothing about reach to all customers.

sections.title: A test result has a limited scope
paragraphs: A test agent can show how the content looks on invited test phones, but does not prove that the agent may contact ordinary customers. Document what the test actually covered and check the public launch separately. The same difference applies to reporting: that one test phone gave a read receipt does not mean the whole target group will later report the same. Testing and production approval answer different questions.

articles.title: How do I state response times in an RCS conversation?
articles.description: Tell the customer when they can expect an answer from staff. An automatic acknowledgment shows that the question arrived, but it should not give the impression that the case is already resolved.

paragraphs: State the times you can actually keep. If the next reply comes during the next staffed shift, say so instead of promising immediate help.
Link the acknowledgment to the case so that staff can pick up where the customer left off. The customer should not have to start a new contact just because the first reply was automatic.

sections.title: A fast auto-reply is not a fast case
paragraphs: If staff reply the next business day, an automatic receipt message should say so instead of implying that help is already under way. State what the customer can do when the matter is urgent. Follow up the actual wait until a useful answer and the time the case was resolved. That shows whether the automation helps the customer or only makes the first technical reply faster.

articles.title: What does an RCS card need from a media URL?
articles.description: The address of an RCS image or file must be retrievable the way the service requires. File type, size and access need to follow the provider's documentation.

paragraphs: An address that only works when you are logged in can fail when the service fetches the image. Also make sure the link does not expire before the message is delivered and does not reveal sensitive information.
Test the final address and the file. Seeing the image in the editor does not test the external fetch.

sections.title: The file must be accessible when it is fetched
paragraphs: An image that works for a logged-in employee can still be unavailable to the messaging service. Check the service's requirements for access, file type and size, and make sure the address does not expire too early. Test with the same published file that will be used in the send. A successful local preview does not prove that the media can be fetched by every part of the delivery flow.

articles.title: Why is an RCS image cropped differently on different phones?
articles.description: The image in an RCS card can be cropped differently depending on the card's layout and the phone. Do not place the most important detail of the product right at the edge.

paragraphs: Test the image on the phones and apps you support. Put price, time and other necessary information in text so that cropping does not remove the message itself.
Review the image together with the headline and buttons. Sometimes a simpler picture is better than trying to fit more into the same image area.

sections.title: Leave room around what matters
paragraphs: Do not place price, product name or other necessary details near the outer edge of the image. The app's display may crop the media differently depending on format and screen. Write the decisive information as text in the message and test the image on several devices. A product image should ideally tolerate variation without making it unclear which option the customer is seeing or what the offer covers.

articles.title: What do I do when the recipient does not support an RCS feature?
articles.description: If a recipient does not support a feature, you need to choose a simpler message or another channel. RCS support in itself does not confirm every carousel or action.

paragraphs: Let the recipient check decide the choice. Keep the information the customer needs even if an image or button is removed.
Test the simpler version too. It should be understandable and usable on its own, without the customer having seen the planned original.

sections.title: Simplify without changing the meaning
paragraphs: If a feature is missing, the content still needs to help the customer with the same task. A carousel can be replaced by a link to comparable options, and a card can become text with a relevant web address. Choose the route based on the capability check and the service's rules. An error in the check should be treated as an error, and it does not give a certain answer that the recipient lacks the feature.

articles.title: How do I detect that RCS events have stopped arriving?
articles.description: Monitor both incoming RCS events and how they are processed. The API can accept a send even when delivery reports or customer replies do not reach your system.

paragraphs: Compare with normal activity and known test flows. A single missing read receipt is not enough to conclude that there is an outage.
Alerts need a recipient. Save identifiers and timestamps so that the person responsible can follow the same message on your side and at the provider.

sections.title: Tell silence from low activity
paragraphs: Few events can be normal if no messages are being sent. Compare the reporting with the sends and test replies that should produce events. Also check errors and queues on the receiving side. A regular check flow with a known expectation can help detect outages, but it should be kept separate from customer statistics so that operational probes are not counted as campaign results.

articles.title: How do I safely resume a stopped RCS flow?
articles.description: After a stop, you first need to see which messages and events have already been processed. Resending the whole list can give customers duplicates.

paragraphs: Read the saved identifiers and statuses. Also check whether the content is still valid; an offer may have expired during the outage.
Resume in smaller steps and follow the outcome. The goal is to close the right cases once, so do not drain the queue at any cost.

sections.title: Resume from a known state
paragraphs: After an outage, some messages may already have been sent while others are still waiting. Examine saved identifiers and statuses before restarting the whole job. Events that are processed again should not create new order changes. Also prioritize relevance: a restored system should not send old reminders just because they were left in the queue. A restart needs both technical and business checks.

articles.title: How does RCS work for customers who use large text?
articles.description: Test RCS cards and buttons with the phone's larger text settings. A preview with standard text does not show how it looks for customers who need larger letters.

paragraphs: Headlines and button labels should still be readable when the lines get more numerous. Important details need to be available as text, not only inside an image.
Follow the link or reply onward as well. It helps little that the card is readable if the booking page does not work with the same settings afterward.

sections.title: Let the content tolerate more space
paragraphs: Large text can make cards longer and push buttons further down. Test a whole message with the phone's larger text setting, and not only the headline. Shorten unnecessary wording but keep terms and important times. The content should be understandable without the customer having to compare a small image caption with a button that has ended up outside the first screen.

articles.title: How do I make RCS understandable with a screen reader?
articles.description: An RCS message needs to be understandable through its text. If only an image states the time or the offer, a screen reader user can miss the message itself.

paragraphs: Write what the button does, for example Open the order. Several buttons labeled Read more give poor guidance when read without the visual context.
Test with a screen reader in the apps your customers use. Support can differ between apps, so any accessibility you promise needs to rest on actual tests.

sections.title: The text must carry the case
paragraphs: Write dates, amounts and instructions as readable text instead of placing them only in an image. Button names like Open the order give more information than Click here. Test with the real messaging app and the phone's screen reader, since support depends on the client. The page the button opens also needs to work; an accessible first text does not help if the next step becomes impossible.

articles.title: What should the first card in an RCS carousel show?
articles.description: The first card needs to explain what the message is about. Some customers will not swipe further, so decisive information must not require a swipe.

paragraphs: Use the following cards for options, such as different products. An important condition or a booked time does not belong only on the last card.
Read only the first card during testing. Can you tell who is sending, what it concerns and what the customer can do?

sections.title: The first card is not the whole message
paragraphs: It should give enough context for the customer to understand why more options exist. Do not put a decisive condition only on a later card. If the first card shows a product, the same comparable details should appear on the others. Send a test and check what is visible before the customer swipes; that is the experience you actually open with.

articles.title: How do I order products in an RCS carousel?
articles.description: Place the products in an order that helps the customer choose. Show the same kind of details in the same place on every card so that comparison is easy.

paragraphs: Product name, description and link should belong together. Avoid mixing a service notice in among the promotional options if it makes the purpose unclear.
Test each link and decide what a fallback SMS needs to say. It cannot reproduce the whole carousel, but it still has to give an understandable message.

sections.title: Choose a sorting that makes sense
paragraphs: Price, category or relevance can be reasonable orders, but they should be consistent and possible to understand. If the cards present different things with no shared details, browsing becomes mostly a search. Also make sure each card can open the right option directly. The order can be tested, but do not conclude that the first card is best only because it got the most views.

articles.title: How many buttons does an RCS message need?
articles.description: The number of buttons should follow the customer's task. A tracking link can be enough for a delivery notice, while a booking may need both Confirm and Request rebooking.

paragraphs: More buttons do not always give more useful choices. If two options seem to do the same thing, they need to be clarified or merged.
The maximum number depends on the format and the service. Check the technical limit, but do not let it become a target for how many buttons you fill in.

sections.title: More choices need clear differences
paragraphs: Add a button when it represents a useful next step of its own. Two nearly identical links often make the choice less clear. A main choice can be complemented with contact or help if the customer needs another route. Test the whole message on a phone and check that the meaning of the buttons is still clear when the text above is longer than in the design draft.

articles.title: When is free text better than reply buttons?
articles.description: Reply buttons suit cases where the options are known. Free text is better when the customer needs to describe a problem, ask their own question or explain something unexpected.
keywords: rcs free text quick reply choice

paragraphs: Let the customer move on if no button choice fits. A wrong choice should not be the only way to get help.
An open question needs someone to handle the reply. Arrange staffing or working automatic handling before you invite free text.

sections.title: Make room for what you did not foresee
paragraphs: Buttons suit a limited choice, while free text is needed when the customer must describe a situation. A dialogue can use both without locking the user into a wrong category. Decide what happens to text that cannot be interpreted with confidence. The customer should get an understandable route to help, and should not see the same button menu again once the problem has turned out to lie outside it.

articles.title: What should the customer see after pressing a button?
articles.description: After a button press, the customer should know what has actually happened. Request rebooking means that a request has been sent, and the new time is still to be booked.

paragraphs: Let the booking or order system decide the confirmation. If handling takes time, confirm receipt and say what happens next.
Test a failed attempt too. The customer needs to know whether the booking is unchanged and how to get help.

sections.title: Confirm the real change
paragraphs: After a choice, the customer needs to know whether something was completed or only passed on. Get the result from the system that owns the case before giving a final answer. If a change is no longer possible, the reply should explain the next step. This is especially important with delayed replies, because the booking or offer may have changed between the message and the button press.

articles.title: How do I choose the language in an RCS send?
articles.description: Choose the language based on what the customer prefers when you have that information. A Swedish phone number does not tell you which language the person wants to read.

paragraphs: Translate all the way through: the message, the buttons and the page or reply afterward. A button in one language helps little if the next step exists only in another.
Longer translations need to be tested on a phone. Shorten where needed, but keep the meaning and the terms.

sections.title: Translate the next step too
paragraphs: A Swedish message that leads to an incomprehensible page gives a fragmented experience. Use the customer's known language choice where there is a relevant basis for it, and keep button texts and confirmations in the same language. If language information is missing, you need a well-considered default. Do not translate stable internal references the way you translate visible text, or the system may have trouble recognizing the customer's action.

articles.title: Where should price and terms go in an RCS offer?
articles.description: Show the price and decisive terms so that the customer understands the offer before the next step. Do not put an important limitation only in a small image caption.

paragraphs: Keep the price together with what is included. If the terms need more space, the link should lead to a clear description that matches the card.
Marketing and purchasing rules apply in RCS too. A limited short format is no reason to leave out information the customer needs.

sections.title: What the customer needs to judge must be visible
paragraphs: If the price applies to a specific period or requires a condition, that should be stated near the offer. A link can give longer information, but should not be used to hide something that changes the main message. Also check the landing page so that the same price and validity apply there. The customer should not have to open several cards to understand which offer is actually being shown.

articles.title: Do emoji suit RCS messages from companies?
articles.description: Emoji can suit business messages when they complement the text. They should not carry a time, a condition or the next step on their own.

paragraphs: Symbols can be displayed and interpreted differently. In a service notice, a clear wording is usually more important than creating the right mood.
Read the message without emoji. If the meaning disappears, the text needs to say more, so add words, not more symbols.

sections.title: Tone must not replace information
paragraphs: Emoji can suit a light-hearted message but should not be the only way to indicate status or meaning. For example, write in text that the booking is confirmed even if a symbol is used. Test how the message reads with a screen reader and on different phones. For delays, payments and errors, a straightforward message is often more helpful than an extra playful touch.

articles.title: How do I make sure an RCS link opens the right order?
articles.description: An order link needs to be tied to the right purchase and the right access. The customer's phone number does not replace the authorization check on the page that opens.

paragraphs: The link should not give access to other customers' orders or details. Use the protection the information requires even when the link has been sent to a known recipient.
Test the right link, a wrong link and an expired link. On an error, the customer should get an understandable message and a route to their case.

sections.title: The right link needs the right authorization
paragraphs: An order reference in the address should not on its own give unauthorized people access to customer details. Plan how the customer is identified and what happens if the link is opened on another device. At the same time, a necessary login should lead back to the right order, and it should never land on the start page. Test several simultaneous orders so that a generic latest-order link does not happen to show the wrong case.

articles.title: Is an RCS preview enough?
articles.description: A preview is enough to review a draft, but it is not enough to approve the whole send. The phone and the messaging app may display the content differently.

paragraphs: Send to real test devices and use the links and replies. Also try long texts, larger text settings and slow image loading.
Include the fallback version. A perfect RCS card does not help a customer who gets an unclear SMS instead.

sections.title: The phone test shows the rest
paragraphs: A preview helps you review content and form, but it does not test the whole delivery or the system behind the buttons. Send tests to real devices and carry out the actions. Also check how the message looks with larger text and a slow connection. An approved draft is one part of quality assurance; working links, customer replies and reporting need tests of their own.

articles.title: How do I write a link in a fallback SMS?
articles.description: Write what the link opens and which case the fallback SMS concerns. Without the RCS card's buttons and images, the text needs to carry more of the context.
keywords: rcs fallback sms button link text

paragraphs: Keep the necessary details such as booking time or order number. The customer may have received only an SMS and should still understand the message.
Check the page the link leads to and how many SMS segments the text produces. A short link says nothing about its safety or clarity.

sections.title: Give the link an understandable purpose
paragraphs: Write why the customer should open the link and which order or booking it concerns. A lone shortened web address can be hard to trust or to tell apart from advertising. Also check the length and encoding of the SMS text once the address has been added. The fallback version should work on its own, since the customer may never have seen the RCS card that the link replaces.

articles.title: Can important information live only in an RCS image?
articles.description: Do not put important information only in an RCS image. It can be cropped, load slowly or be hard to read on a small screen.

paragraphs: Write time, price and terms as plain text. Let the image show the product or what is easier to explain visually.
Remove the image when you review the message. If the case or the next step cannot be understood, the text needs to be supplemented.

sections.title: An image can fail to appear or be hard to read
paragraphs: Slow connections, cropping and assistive tools can affect how the image is perceived. Do not put the booking time, price or terms only in the media. Write the core information as text and let the image explain or supplement it. That also helps when a simpler format has to be used. The customer should be able to understand the important message without having to enlarge small graphic text.

articles.title: When is video useful in an RCS message?
articles.description: Video works when motion explains something, for example how a product is used. A short status update rarely needs a film.

paragraphs: Give the essential information in text too. The customer may not be able to play a video right then, and the service has to support the file.
Test the file on a phone and see how it loads. Choose the length and format based on what needs to be shown, and leave the available space out of the decision.

sections.title: Choose video when the motion is needed
paragraphs: A short instruction or a product in use can be easier to understand on film than in several still images. A delivery time or a simple price rarely needs video. Make the message understandable without sound and check how it loads on a phone. If the customer has to watch the film to find a basic detail, the medium has probably taken too large a role in the message.

articles.title: How do I use customer names without embarrassing mistakes?
articles.description: Use a customer's name when the data is reliable. A greeting with the wrong name or a visible system field can make the rest of the message hard to trust.

paragraphs: Have a neutral greeting for when the name is missing. Test the import with empty fields and check that order details are not mixed up between customers.
Personal does not have to mean named. A correct message about the customer's case can feel more considerate than an uncertain "Hi" followed by a first name.

sections.title: Have text that works without a name
paragraphs: Customer data can be empty, outdated or contain a company name where you expected a first name. Only use names when the quality and context are good enough. Write a fallback greeting that works without the field and try incomplete records before sending. A correct order reference often helps more than a personal tone, and a wrong name can reduce trust in the whole message.

articles.title: How does the customer recognize the company in a long RCS conversation?
articles.description: Keep the same recognizable business profile throughout the conversation and state which case each new message concerns. A name and a logo do not give the full context.

paragraphs: Mark when the conversation moves on to a new question. Avoid mixing an ongoing support problem with offers that do not belong there.
When staff change, the next person should be able to continue the case. The customer does not need to know your departments to understand the reply.

sections.title: Keep the context when the topic changes
paragraphs: A long thread can contain several orders or questions. State which order or case a new message concerns, without repeating the whole history. If staff take over from the automation, the customer should understand who is now replying. The profile gives a shared identity, but the text still needs to separate a new offer from a follow-up on an ongoing question.

articles.title: Does the whole purchase have to happen in the RCS chat?
articles.description: The whole purchase does not have to happen in the RCS chat. A button can open a website where the customer pays, books or completes the order.

paragraphs: Say what the button opens. "Buy now" can be misleading if it only leads to information, while "Open the product page" describes the actual step.
Check the landing page on a phone and keep the offer the same in both places. Measure the purchase where it is completed, and look beyond the click in the message.

sections.title: The inbox can be the start
paragraphs: RCS can gather a message and a clear next step without building the whole purchase in the chat. A web page can still be better for login, payment or many product choices. Make sure the handover keeps the customer's context and that it is clear when the next step is done. Fewer app installations are a feature of the setup and do not prove that every customer journey gets shorter.

articles.title: How does an RCS bot hand over to a human?
articles.description: When automatic replies do not help, the customer needs to be able to reach staff. Confirm the handover and stop asking the same question if the customer has already answered.

paragraphs: Pass on the relevant conversation history and case number with appropriate access. Then the person taking over can continue without the customer having to start again.
State a response time that your staffing can meet. An automatic reply should not pretend to come from a human.

sections.title: Hand over the question and the customer together
paragraphs: Staff need to see what the customer has already chosen and which case the conversation is about. Say when the handover happens and what the customer can expect while waiting. If no one is staffing the channel, another way to make contact should be available. A bot that keeps sending the same menu while a person replies easily causes confusion, so decide who owns the conversation after the handover.

articles.title: How do I write a good error message in RCS?
articles.description: A useful error message says what went wrong and how the customer can move forward. An internal error number needs an explanation.

paragraphs: Say whether the booking or order is unchanged. There is a difference between a request that did not arrive and one that was received but could not be completed.
Offer a relevant way to get in touch or a link. Do not ask the customer to tap again if that could create a second order or a duplicate case.

sections.title: Explain what the customer can do now
paragraphs: The customer rarely needs an internal error code, but does need to know whether the request was received and whether anything changed. If the outcome is uncertain, do not ask the person to repeat a sensitive choice without a check. Give a way to get in touch or a safe retry that fits the situation. Keep technical details in the operations documentation and the practical consequence in the customer's message.

articles.title: How do I make recurring RCS messages less disruptive?
articles.description: Send a new message when something relevant has changed for the customer. Every internal update does not have to become a notification.

paragraphs: Combine messages that would otherwise arrive close together and sound almost the same. Say what is new, and avoid only saying that the order has been updated.
Keep marketing choices separate from service information. The aim is for the customer to get the right message, which is a different goal from sending as many messages as the system can produce.

sections.title: Send when the information changes something
paragraphs: Several status changes in your system can mean the same thing to the customer. Combine them where you can and prioritize messages that require an action or give new useful information. Let the recipient's choices govern relevant recurring messages. Follow up complaints and blocking signals together with delivery data, because a high delivery rate does not tell you whether the contact is appreciated.

articles.title: Which time should a scheduled RCS send use?
articles.description: Find out which time zone the scheduling uses. UTC and Swedish local time differ, and the difference changes with summer and winter time.
keywords: rcs schedule time zone daylight saving

paragraphs: State the date and time unambiguously according to the service's documentation. A booking time in the message should be the time the customer is expected to follow, and an internal system time does not serve that purpose.
Try the schedule before a larger send. For recipients in several countries, you also need to judge whether the same send time makes sense locally.

sections.title: Decide which local time is meant
paragraphs: A send planned for the morning needs to be tied to the right time zone and handle the switch between summer and winter time. Follow the service's rules for time values and save the plan so it can be checked. Test edge cases before recurring jobs start. A correctly stored time is not enough if the business and the integration have different ideas about when the customer should be contacted.

articles.title: How do I run a fair A/B test of RCS text?
articles.description: A fair A/B test compares one limited change across equivalent groups. If you change the text, the offer and the send time at once, the cause of any difference stays unclear.

paragraphs: Decide what counts before sending. If the goal is bookings, completed bookings should be the main measure, and clicks alone are not enough.
Report reach and the use of fallback channels as well. Groups with different delivery conditions can give a misleading comparison of the text itself.

sections.title: Make the groups comparable
paragraphs: If the audience, the offer and the button text all change at once, you cannot know what affected the result. Distribute equivalent recipients and keep the follow-up period the same. Decide on a relevant measure in advance, for example completed bookings. A small test can give a direction, but it needs to be reported with its size and uncertainty, and should not be presented as a general RCS effect.

articles.title: How do I keep several order messages together in RCS?
articles.description: Write the order number or another relevant reference and what has changed. "Your order is ready" can be unclear to a customer with several orders in the same chat.

paragraphs: Fetch the status from the order system and link to the right order. Do not add personal data that is not needed to understand the message.
Coordinate automatic notifications with staff replies. If the customer has been told there is a problem, the next standard message should not contradict it.

sections.title: Identify the order at every important step
paragraphs: A customer can have several simultaneous orders from the same sender. A short reference and the right tracking link help tell the messages apart. Keep internal delivery events tied to the same order so that a late status message does not give wrong information. The thread gathers the contact with the company, but it should not replace a clear link between message and case.

articles.title: How do I keep the same message in RCS and SMS?
articles.description: RCS and SMS need to say the same important thing, but with different design. RCS can have an image and buttons, while SMS needs text and a plain link.

paragraphs: Check the date, price, status and terms in both versions. The fallback must not fetch older information than the original.
Read the versions separately. The customer should understand the one that arrives without needing to know the other.

sections.title: Same information, different presentation
paragraphs: RCS can show images and buttons, while SMS needs text and a plain link. Keep the case, the terms and the next step in both versions, even when the form changes. Review them together when the offer is updated. If only one version gets a new price or time window, the fallback channel can give a different message from the main channel to customers in the same send.

articles.title: What do I do when a customer objects to RCS advertising?
articles.description: According to IMY, a customer has an absolute right to object to processing for direct marketing. After the objection, the personal data must no longer be used for that purpose.

paragraphs: Stop the sends in all affected lists and tools. It is not enough to add a note at support if the next campaign still uses the number.

Service cases can have different legal bases and need to be assessed separately. Get help from someone with data protection expertise on where to draw the line in your setup. This is an overview and does not constitute legal advice.

sections.title: The objection has to reach the whole flow
paragraphs: Marking the customer in one register does not help if a copied campaign list can still be sent. Stop relevant planned advertising sends and make sure connected services use the updated information. Keep the difference between marketing and necessary service messages clear. Confirm receipt in plain language and have someone with data protection expertise assess how the basis for the objection should be handled.

articles.title: Is an RCS reply consent to advertising?
articles.description: A reply about a booking is not in itself consent to advertising. The customer may want to confirm a time without wanting to receive future offers.

paragraphs: Neither delivery status nor read receipts show a marketing choice. Assess the contact rules and the processing of personal data for their respective purposes.
If you ask for such a choice, state clearly what the customer is agreeing to and handle it separately from the booking. The conditions need to be assessed for the specific situation.

sections.title: Assess what the customer actually chose
paragraphs: A reply to a booking question or a click to track a parcel describes that specific action. It is not automatically approval of new offers. If you ask for a marketing choice, the meaning needs to be clear and the documentation should show which choice was made. Technical button data can help register the event, but it does not replace the assessment under the contact rules.

articles.title: How should RCS advertising be labeled?
articles.description: Advertising in RCS must be recognizable as advertising, and the responsible sender must be clear. An offer should not be designed as if it were a necessary order message.

paragraphs: Use the company name and a text that shows the purpose. A verified profile does not replace a clear description of the message as advertising.
Price, terms and claims also need to be correct. The whole offer is assessed, and the labeling is only one part of it.

sections.title: The profile does not replace advertising identification
paragraphs: A company name shows who the conversation comes from but does not always tell you that a particular message is advertising. Design the content so that the purpose and the sender can be understood. Also review where the link leads and that the offer matches there. A service-style appearance should not be used to hide an advertising message, so assess the real content and context of the text.

articles.title: Can an order message also contain advertising?
articles.description: Sending a necessary order message does not automatically give you the right to add advertising. Delivery information and a new offer have different purposes.

paragraphs: Assess the contact rules for the advertising part separately. It must also not make the order information harder to find.
Keep marketing choices separate from the case. A customer who has objected to advertising should not get it baked into a delivery update.

sections.title: Assess the addition separately
paragraphs: An order message is needed for the purchase, while a new offer can have a different purpose and different conditions for contact. Putting them on the same card does not make the difference smaller. Review which information is necessary for the case and what is marketing. When in doubt, it is better to keep the flows clearly separate and get a legal assessment than to assume that the whole message is service.

articles.title: How do I stop advertising at all sending providers?
articles.description: The opt-out has to reach every tool that controls the company's marketing sends. Otherwise the customer can be stopped in one service and remain in another.

paragraphs: Decide which system holds the current block status and how it is passed on. Review imports so that an older list does not reactivate a blocked number.
Test the whole path from the opt-out to the next send list. The confirmation in the chat is not enough if the advertising continues.

sections.title: Have one shared source for contact choices
paragraphs: If several services send, they need to get the same message about an objection. Also check exported lists and scheduled jobs created before the choice changed. Test with a controlled contact that the stop takes effect everywhere advertising can be sent. A successful opt-out in a single portal does not show that the other providers or the manual sends have been updated.

articles.title: Which customer details are needed in an RCS flow?
articles.description: An RCS flow needs the customer details that are relevant to the case, and a copy of the whole customer profile is more than that. An order ID can be enough to find the rest in the customer system.

paragraphs: Phone numbers and replies can be personal data. Assess the purpose, access and retention time for the data that is sent and stored.
Check with your data protection work and the provider's terms. Do not include an extra field just because the API can receive it.

sections.title: Start from what the case requires
paragraphs: A delivery message can need a phone number and an order reference without the whole customer profile following to the messaging service. Map which fields are sent, stored and visible to staff. Remove unnecessary data before it leaves the source system. How much data is needed depends on the purpose. IMY's information on objections is important, but on its own it is not a complete guide to this assessment.

articles.title: How long should RCS replies be stored?
articles.description: No single retention period fits all RCS replies. How long they are needed depends on the case, the purpose and the requirements that apply to the business.

paragraphs: An active support question, compiled statistics and a technical log can need different handling. The whole conversation does not need to exist for the same length of time in every system.
Decide who deletes and how it works in exports and at providers. Have someone with data protection expertise assess the periods for your setup.

sections.title: Set the time by purpose, and leave habit out of it
paragraphs: Customer replies can be needed during an ongoing case but should not automatically stay forever in several systems. Decide who is responsible for deletion and how copies in exports, logs and provider services are handled. A single general time limit does not necessarily suit all data. Document the need and get a data protection assessment, and do not assume that the messaging channel's default setting is enough.

articles.title: Who should be allowed to read customers' RCS replies?
articles.description: Customers' RCS replies should be accessible to those who need them in their work. The fact that a system receives the replies does not mean that all employees should be able to read them.

paragraphs: Customer service may need the conversation text, while technical troubleshooting can sometimes manage with status and identifiers. Adapt access to the task.
Remove or change permissions when staff leave or change roles. Also make sure you know in which tools the conversations are stored.

sections.title: Access should follow the work task
paragraphs: Someone troubleshooting delivery may need status and identifiers but not the customer's whole document. Separate operational data from content where possible and let the responsible teams see the relevant material. Also plan what happens when staff change roles. The channel's access rules are only one part, and copies in case systems and exports need the same careful handling.

articles.title: What do I do if a customer sends sensitive information?
articles.description: If a customer sends sensitive information, follow the business's procedures for that information. The fact that the data was sent voluntarily does not make further spreading or long storage appropriate.

paragraphs: Do not ask for more than the case requires. If needed, move the continuation to a more secure, suitable channel and avoid having the content copied into general logs.
Assess both data protection and security. A verified sender says who is sending, and it does not describe how the customer's reply is protected in your systems.

sections.title: Steer onward without spreading the content
paragraphs: If the customer sends more sensitive information than the case needs, it should not automatically be repeated in auto-replies or broad logs. Assess who has to handle it and give the customer a suitable protected route when needed. Private RCS encryption says nothing certain about the protection in the company's inbox or storage. The handling therefore needs to be based on the data and the real systems.

articles.title: Why do RCS statistics change after a send?
articles.description: RCS statistics can change as new delivery and read events arrive. A report pulled right after a send is therefore not always the final picture.

paragraphs: Check which time fields and report periods your service uses. Send time, activity time and the time the report was generated can differ.
Compare reports at equivalent points in time and note when each one was pulled. A growing number of reads does not mean more messages were sent.

sections.title: Use the same follow-up time
paragraphs: Delivery and read events can arrive after the first report has been pulled. If two campaigns are measured at different times, the comparison is misleading. Save the report time and define when a result counts as mature enough. Keep late channel events separate from bookings or purchases that can also happen later. They change different parts of the analysis and should not be mixed together.

articles.title: How do I tell an RCS click from a purchase?
articles.description: A click in RCS shows that the customer chose an action. A purchase is a later result that has to be confirmed where the order is completed.

paragraphs: Link the follow-up to the right send using relevant identifiers. If sales is the goal, an opened product page should not be counted as a completed purchase.
Report clicks and purchases separately. That way you can see both the interest in the message and how many people completed the next step.

sections.title: Connect events without overstating
paragraphs: A click can open the page without the customer completing anything. Measure the desired action where it happens and define how it is linked to the send. Handle repeated clicks and the same purchase so they do not turn into several results. Also report when the link is uncertain. The channel report and the order register data are two different sources, and the two are not different names for the same measure.

articles.title: Can I compare RCS reads with SMS deliveries?
articles.description: RCS reads and SMS deliveries are different measures and should not be compared as if they meant the same thing. A delivery report does not say the customer has read the message.

paragraphs: If possible, choose a shared outcome, such as confirmed bookings. Show each channel's reach, cost and status metrics next to it.
You need definitions and comparable groups to reach a useful conclusion. Otherwise more reported events may simply mean that one channel can measure more.

sections.title: Choose a shared end metric
paragraphs: RCS reads and SMS deliveries describe different steps and should not be set against each other as equivalent results. A completed purchase or a booking can be more comparable if the offer and the audience are kept the same. Report which channel events exist and which are missing. That makes it possible to see both differences in reporting and real differences in what customers do, without mixing them up.

articles.title: What should customer service measure in RCS?
articles.description: Customer service should measure whether the customer gets help, and whether the reply is read is only part of that. Time to a meaningful reply and the share of closed cases can be relevant metrics.
keywords: rcs customer service metrics response time

paragraphs: Decide what a closed case means for you. An automatic greeting resolves no question, and a button may only send a request.
Use data from the case system together with RCS status. That makes it easier to tell waiting for delivery apart from waiting for actual help.

sections.title: Measure help, with activity as only one input
paragraphs: Many messages or fast auto-replies say little about whether the customer's problem was solved. Track time to a useful reply, the resolution and any new contact about the same case. Separate automatic replies from the work of your staff. Also read a relevant sample of cases qualitatively, with appropriate access, so the report does not reward a dialogue that looks fast but leaves the customer with the same question.

articles.title: How do I calculate the cost when RCS has an SMS fallback?
articles.description: Budget for RCS and the SMS fallback according to the service's own terms. A fallback SMS is not necessarily included in the price just because the send looks like one continuous flow.

paragraphs: Find out when billing happens and whether the SMS text is split into several parts. Also clarify which status or time limit triggers the fallback.
Then calculate for the whole send and its outcome. An RCS price on its own does not explain the cost for customers reached through different channels.

sections.title: Calculate each channel separately
