paragraphs: Start from how many messages of each type are actually billed and which ones move on to the fallback. Delivery reports can help you follow the flow but do not replace the service's price terms. Reconcile the invoice data and state whether the cost also includes integration or handling. An average per contact can otherwise hide that the same customer received several messages or that the fallback cost was counted twice.

articles.title: Is a delivery report also an invoice report?
articles.description: A delivery report shows the status of a message. An invoice report shows what was billed under the agreement. The two reports answer different questions.

paragraphs: Read which events and message types are billable. The words accepted and delivered do not decide the price. The service's definitions do.
Link the records using message IDs when the totals need to be followed up. If the invoice deviates, ask for an explanation at record level, and a new total figure alone is not enough.

sections.title: Technical status and payment rule are different things
paragraphs: An invoice can be based on other rules than the status you show in a customer case. Ask the provider to explain what is billed for an accepted request, for errors and for any fallback channel. Link the data using identifiers where possible, but keep the different definitions. If the reports do not match, the difference needs to be investigated, and renaming every status to billed would only hide it.

articles.title: Which customers should be part of an RCS pilot?
articles.description: A pilot should include customers who fit the chosen use case and may be contacted. Internal test phones with the best possible support alone can give too narrow a basis.

paragraphs: Include relevant variations in phones and apps. Also try the path for recipients who lack RCS or one of the features.

Decide the questions before the test: does the customer understand the message, does the reply work and does the case end up in the right place? That tells you more than confirming that the message could be sent.

sections.title: Let the sample test the real risks
paragraphs: Start with recipients you are allowed to contact and who represent the phones and customer cases you need to handle. Add controlled test cases without support and with delayed replies. A sample made up only of employees with the same phone can give an overly positive picture. Document who was included and which situations are missing before the pilot's results are used to plan a larger send.

articles.title: When should an RCS pilot be paused?
articles.description: Pause a pilot if customer data turns out wrong, unsubscribing fails or a reply is linked to the wrong case. An accepted API call does not make up for such errors.

paragraphs: Appoint someone responsible and set the stop conditions in advance. When you stop, you also need to see which messages have already been sent and which are waiting.
Fix the cause and test the same case before you continue. The pilot's limited size exists to catch errors before more customers are affected.

sections.title: Set stop criteria before the start
paragraphs: Wrong recipients, broken links and duplicate changes are examples of deviations that can call for a pause before more customers are affected. Decide who makes the call and how scheduled messages are stopped. A low click rate is a different kind of signal than a security fault. After a pause, you should be able to tell messages already sent from pending jobs before the pilot is resumed.

articles.title: What should I ask an RCS provider before buying?
articles.description: Ask an RCS provider to show how your own flow works: which customers you can reach, how the sender is approved and how content, replies and the fallback channel are handled.

paragraphs: Clarify prices and what is actually activated for your account. A general feature list can include things you do not have access to yet.
Ask for terms on data handling, support and integration. A test with your own messages gives a better basis for a decision than a general promise about coverage.

sections.title: Ask for answers that can be tested
paragraphs: A demonstration of an attractive card does not answer questions about delivery, customer replies or operations. Ask the provider to show how your planned content works for relevant recipients and how an error is handled. Billing and fallback terms should be clear before you make the calculation. Distinguish between what is included now, what requires account activation and what exists only on a future roadmap.

articles.title: How do companies test reach to iPhone?
articles.description: Test iPhone reach with the company's registered sender and the service you will use. A private RCS chat between two people does not test the same thing.

paragraphs: Use the provider's recipient checks and send the intended content to real test devices. Also check that business messages are allowed in the recipient's settings.
Describe which phones and subscriptions the test covered. A successful delivery to one iPhone gives no certain answer for all Swedish iPhone customers.

sections.title: Test from the right sender
paragraphs: A private RCS conversation on iPhone shows that this particular conversation works. For business reach, the test needs to use the launched agent, relevant content and recipients with different subscriptions. Save capability results and delivery events as separate records. A small test can verify specific combinations, but it should not be reported as a coverage share for all Swedish iPhone users.

articles.title: How do I interpret a news item about an RCS launch?
articles.description: An RCS news item has to be read in its context: country, carrier, phone and type of use. Support for private Android chat is no statement about business sends to iPhone.

paragraphs: Check the date and the official source. An announced pilot or upcoming launch is different from a feature available to all customers.
If the messages differ, keep the uncertainty in your planning. Ask the carrier or your sending provider about the reach your particular campaign needs.

sections.title: Read the scope behind the headline
paragraphs: A launch news item can apply to private chat, one country, one app or certain subscriptions. Check those limits before the news becomes a claim about your customer reach. See whether business senders are mentioned explicitly and follow up with current support information. A future rollout is different from support today, and a marketing claim still needs concrete evidence for the recipients you want to reach.

articles.title: What should I check when the business profile changes?
articles.description: A change to the company name or RCS profile may require a new review under the service's rules. You cannot assume an approved sender is free to change brand.

paragraphs: Reconcile the change with your partner and update contact details, templates and links. After a new profile, the old name should not linger in the next step.
Try the profile in a real conversation. The customer needs to recognize the sender, and verification is about identity and authorization as well as the logo file.

sections.title: Check more than the image
paragraphs: With a new name or logo, links, support address and registration details also need to match the customer's expectations. Ask your partner whether the change affects verification or launch. Then send a test so that the public profile is reviewed as well as the editing view. Old messages and new notices can sit in the same thread, so explain a larger brand change when the customer might otherwise become unsure.

sections.title: New logo shape in Google Messages
paragraphs: Google Messages now shows a business logo as a rounded square instead of a circle. Private individuals keep round pictures, so businesses stand out more clearly in the inbox. A verified sender gets a checkmark after the name.
points: The logo should be square, 224 × 224 px, without rounded corners of its own.
Use a solid background. A transparent logo is hard to see, especially in dark mode.
Leave some space around the logo so nothing is cropped at the corners.
Existing senders must have switched logo by June 1, 2027. The change is reviewed in the same way as other changes.

articles.title: Should support and marketing use the same RCS sender?
articles.description: Support and marketing may need the same recognizable RCS identity when they represent the same brand. The organization's internal boundaries do not have to be visible to the customer.

paragraphs: Keep permissions and marketing choices clear all the same. A support case should not be interrupted by a campaign the customer has opted out of.
Ask the provider how one shared agent or several agents can be used. Choose what fits the customer's contact with the company and the rules the service sets.

sections.title: Coordinate the contact behind the profile
paragraphs: A shared sender can give recognition, but the teams need to know who is responsible for replies and which contact choices apply. A campaign send must not leave support with questions they have no background for. If several agents are used, the split should make sense to the customer. The organization chart does not need to show up in the inbox, and clear case handling matters more than giving each department its own profile.

articles.title: What should be checked before a customer list is used for RCS?
articles.description: Check phone numbers, duplicates and current opt-outs before a customer list is used. The recipients also need to be allowed to be contacted for the purpose of the send.

paragraphs: An old import must not overwrite a newer unsubscribe. Make sure the right order details belong to the right number if the content is personalized per customer.
Try a small part first. The fact that the file can be imported says nothing about whether the numbers support RCS or whether the send is allowed.

sections.title: A clean list takes more than the right format
paragraphs: Check duplicates, current numbers and which contacts may be included for the purpose of this particular send. An export can be older than the latest objection, so you need to reconcile against current contact choices. Keep traceability to the list's origin without carrying over more personal data than necessary. A successful file import test only shows that the records can be read, and says nothing about whether they may be used.

articles.title: How may customer results be described in RCS marketing?
articles.description: Customer results need to be verifiable. Describe what was measured and in which campaign, and avoid turning a single figure into a promise for all customers.

paragraphs: Separate clicks from purchases and state how a comparison was made. A logo is no evidence for a results claim.
Use customer names and references you have the right to show. If you have no customer case, you can give a clearly labeled example, but you cannot invent a customer's experience.

sections.title: Separate a logo from a measured result
paragraphs: A customer logo shows a relationship when its use is permitted, and it is no evidence for a particular click rate or sales increase. Results claims need documentation, a period, a sample and a metric definition. Describe a single outcome as exactly that, a single outcome. If the comparison is missing, you should not write that RCS caused the improvement. Publication also needs to be cleared with the customer.

articles.title: How do I keep information about RCS support up to date?
articles.description: Information about RCS support needs a date for the check and a clear source. An old launch news item is not always enough for a current answer.

paragraphs: Follow the official carrier and platform pages. Keep private chat separate from business reach and note when sources say different things.
Change the check date only when the information has actually been checked again. A new date without a new check makes the information more misleading, and no more current.

sections.title: Record what changed
paragraphs: A routine for carrier information should note the source, the time of the check and which use case the information applies to. If two original sources differ, that should be visible until the difference can be explained. Update the limitations as well as the yes or no. For business RCS, the documentation needs to be supplemented with tests from your own agent, since general consumer support does not report that reach.

articles.title: How do I test RCS between two carriers?
articles.description: Test with two phones that have working RCS and different carriers. Check the connection status on both before you start.

paragraphs: Send a simple text and read which channel was used. Then try the image or the feature you want to examine. If something fails, change one condition at a time.
Note the app, system version, carrier and time, without spreading private conversations. The result applies to the tested pair and says nothing about all subscriptions or business senders.

sections.title: Keep the combinations clear
paragraphs: Test a new message in each direction and note the phone, app, subscription and channel text. A successful test in one combination does not mean all phones on the same network work the same way. If someone changes app or line, the test needs to be described again. Report only the combinations that were actually tried, and keep private conversations separate from tests of business senders.
